abstract: A least squares estimation algorithm for the azimuth and elevation angles as well as range of a single near-field source impinging on a uniform circular array is proposed. By exploiting the centro-symmetric array configuration, two correlation functions are devised to obtain their closed-form estimates. It is shown that the proposed method gives comparable estimation performance with that of the conventional MUSIC scheme but the former is much computationally simple.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband three-way power divider using modified microstrip-slotline
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel three-way power divider with a broadband (4 to 9 GHz) performance is presented. The proposed power divider utilizes a modified broadband slot-coupling configuration in the ground. For verification, the measured results of less than 1.2 dB insertion loss, better than 13 dB return loss and almost 10 dB isolation across the whole operating band, are also given, which show basic agreement to the simulation results.

articleTitle: River boundaries extraction in mountain areas for SAR images with fusing GIS information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: River boundaries extraction on SAR images is valuable for flood monitoring. Traditional methods usually failed in high relief areas. We proposed a river boundaries extraction method to conquer the difficulty to discriminate rivers from mountain shadows through fusing GIS information.

articleTitle: Joint feature selection and classifier design for radar targets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A joint feature selection and classifier design is proposed in this paper. The approach adopts the feature dimension extension by power transformation as a new kernel function, which can not only make full use of the input samples to form the nonlinear classification boundary, but also realize the nonlinear feature selection. A zero-mean Gaussian prior with Gamma precision is used to promote sparsity in utilization of features in our model. The experiments based on a measured radar data set demonstrate the practicability and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on low-angle altitude measurement of slow target
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Computation method of complex monopulse ratio based on multipath effect is discussed. Through analyzing the principle of low-angle altitude measurement which bases on multipath effect of step swept frequency, a new low-angle altitude measurement method is developed, which uses multipath varying effect of real part of complex monopulse ratio during step swept frequency. Simulation shows that this new method is effective for low-angle altitude measurement for the slow target.

articleTitle: Knowledge-aided Bayesian Rao and wald tests for radar adaptive detection in heterogeneous environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We resort to a Bayesian framework and design knowledge-aided (KA) Rao and Wald tests for radar adaptive detection based on the partially homogeneous model, which outperform their conventional counterparts in heterogeneous environment. Meanwhile, the coincidence of the proposed detectors is proved.

articleTitle: An analysis and research on composite modulation algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of Doppler spread caused by high-speed target motion during coherent accumulation period for linear FM signals, then a Dual linear FM composite algorithm is proposed. The theory analysis and simulation are presented, and the conventional processing algorithm is compared with the proposed algorithm based on the echoed signal. The results shows that the composite algorithm is useful and able to be realized in engineering.

articleTitle: A Linear Frequency Modulated bistatic radar for on-the-ground object detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A radar system for detecting and localizing small targets on the ground is proposed in this paper. The system transmits wideband Linear Frequency Modulated pulses from ground-based transmitter. The reflected pulses will be collected simultaneously by two different ground-based receivers installed in different bistatic positions. Accurate range processing in this bistatic configuration will lead us to detect small objects like N-type connectors in several meters distances.

articleTitle: Accuracy of height estimation by a system of 2-D netted radars
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: 3-D target position estimation can be obtained by a system of 2-D netted radars performing a suitable fusion of the 2-D plots or tracks from the different located radars. In this paper we discuss the performance of different systems of 2-D netted radars in terms of accuracy of the height estimation. In particular the difference between a monostatic and bistatic system will be investigated.

articleTitle: An approach for sparse baselines SAR tomography
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper deals with the synthetic aperture radar tomography (Tomo-SAR), which is a potential technique for three-dimensional SAR imaging by synthesizing the SAR images of the same area to an aperture in the vertical direction. However, the conventional Fourier-based methods are limited capable for the sparse baselines cases. In this paper, the Tomo-SAR with sparse baselines is formulated as a sparse signal recovery problem. Then, by solving it, the super-resolution imaging in elevation direction is obtained. The feasibility of the proposed approach is validated by results obtained from simulations with sparse baselines.

articleTitle: System errors estimation of DOA and TDOA jointed locating system using sequential least squares
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To estimate system errors of direction of arrival (DOA) and time difference of arrival (TDOA) with two stations locating system, a system error estimation model is build through analyzing the locating principle. In succession sequential least squares estimation (SLSE) is studied. And then he estimation process is given. At last convergence and accuracy of SLSE are researched through Monte Carlo simulation. And target tracks which are before and after the bias registration are compared. Theoretical analyses and simulation shows that the SLSE can exactly and effectively estimate system errors of DOA and TDOA locating system.

Author Keywords: direction of arrival and time difference of arrival jointed locating system

articleTitle: A modified DPA for weak target detection via HPRF radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To address the problem of weak target detection when range ambiguity exists and the trajectory is discontinuous, a modified DPA via revising state transitions is proposed in this paper. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Robust covariance matrix estimation in radar array processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Recently, several robust covariance matrix estimation techniques were proposed, such as normalized sample covariance matrix (NSCM) and fixed point matrix (FPM). They were claimed to be able to provide better performance for non-Gaussian clutter or in the presence of disturbance. In this paper, the performance of these robust covariance matrix estimators were evaluated and compared with the conventional sample covariance matrix (SCM) technique using both simulated and experimental data, in terms of target direction estimation accuracy and clutter suppression capability in space-time adaptive processing (STAP).

articleTitle: Kullback leibler estimation of distribution parameters for SAR data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: It is essential for SAR automatic target recognition (ATR) to estimate the parameters of statistical modes in SAR images. Most studies have relied on the conventional methods, such as moments technique and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method. In this paper, we apply a Kullback Leibler (KL) method to parameters estimation for SAR data. The ant colony algorithm (ACA) is extended to search for the optimal parameters. Experiment results show that the KL method performs better than MLE method in all cases tested.

articleTitle: Research on detection of hypersonic weak target
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For the problem of range migration due to fast moving of the target, a novel coherent integration method based on Fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) is presented. Using the scale transform character of FRFT, the proposed method can accomplish scale transform at the same time of coherent integration, which can correct range migration, and all pulses can achieve effective accumulation in accumulation time. As a result, it is proved that this method improves the detection performance of hypersonic target greatly, and reduces the demand of the input SNR.

articleTitle: Automatic target detection in search and rescue based on Yamaguchi polarimetric decomposition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Based on the analysis of the polarization scattering characteristics of aircraft targets, using aircraft tail dihedral returns strong double-bounce and helix scattering signatures, a novel method of automatic target detection for crashed aircraft based on Yamaguchi polarimetric decomposition is proposed.

articleTitle: A novel elliptical UWB antenna with dual band-notched characteristics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An elliptical UWB antenna owns two rejected bands is proposed in this paper. Two kinds of slots, a U-shaped slot etched on the background and two L-shaped slots etched on the radiating patch, are introduced. The U-shaped slot produces a notched-band at 3.5GHz, while the L-shaped slots present a notched band at 5.15-5.85GHz. Besides, a double-fed structure and a coupled-line-fed structure is also applied. The double-fed branches balance the currents on the patch, and the two rectangular patches of the coupled-line-fed structure could enhance the VSWR at notched-bands while reduce the VSWR at passed-bands. The structure of the proposed antenna is very novel.

articleTitle: Clutter suppression for bistatic airborne radar with range ambiguity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Bistatic pulse-Doppler airborne radar has desirable properties such as low probability of intercept relative to its monostatic counterpart, however the clutter characteristics of bistatic airborne radar are more complex than those of monostatic airborne radar, and the clutter spectra not only vary severely with range, but also vary with bistatic configuration. In this paper, the geometry model and clutter spectrum distribution in space-time plane of bistatic airborne radar are given, respectively, and a novel clutter suppression method for bistatic airborne radar with range ambiguity is presented. The simulation results illustrate the performance improvement achieved for bistatic airborne radar.

articleTitle: A RFI suppression approach based on along-track interferometric image
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) will influence the interferometric image easier than the amplitude image in the Very High Frequency/Ultra High Frequency (VHF/UHF) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). In this paper, a simpler detector with binary hypothesis is constructed with the discussion of the thresholds. Based on this, a new interference suppression method based on azimuth-time range-spectrum domain of along-track interferometric image is proposed. The approach is effective for ground moving target detection in real-time processing and its performance is testified by simulation data.

articleTitle: A novel despeckling algorithm of polarimetric SAR image based on SNR and parameter-vector spectrum amendment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The subspace filtering of polarimetric SAR image can retain polarimetric signature very well, but for its limitations it is necessary to enhance its despeckling effect. So a novel despeckling algorithm of polarimetric SAR image based on SNR and parameter-vector spectrum amendment is proposed. First, the sufficient and necessary condition of signal-noise separation based on subspace filtering is analyzed to conclude that signal is not completely separated from noise, so a new despeckling tactic based on SNR is produced, which means preserving components with high SNR and discarding components with low SNR. Then, for the defect of reconstructing parameter vector in the subspace filtering, a method of parameter-vector spectrum amendment is derived, which can enhance despeckling effect and keep the filtered polarimetric data close to the unfiltered. At last, the experiment shows that the novel algorithm definitely has better despeckling effect than the subspace filtering, and retains edge-point feature and polarimetric signature as well.

articleTitle: A method for ISAR imaging of high speed moving target based on phase-coded signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel method for high speed moving targets ISAR imaging is presented in this paper. The phase-coded signal bears favorable resolution in range and velocity, however it is sensitive to Doppler frequency, the Doppler phase should be repaired before the pulse compression. For the high moving target, the envelop stretch must be considered especially. A movement compensation method which combines wideband phase-coded signal and narrow band linear frequency modulated signal is introduced. The narrow band signal is applied for detection and measurement, while the wideband signal for improving the speed accuracy and imaging. The flow chart of the compensation method for phase-coded signal imaging of high speed moving target is given. Simulation shows the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Maneuvering target tracking using IMMPF in Passive Coherent Location radar with glint noise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of maneuvering target tracking in Passive Coherent Location (PCL) radar with glint noise. An Interacting Multiple Model Particle Filtering (IMMPF) method using Time-of-Arrival (TOA) measurements is proposed. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Research on cellular radar for low-flying small targets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper explores the feasibility of the cellular radar with the mobile base station illuminator for detecting the low-flying small targets. First it analyses the choice of illuminator, available signal for cellular radar. Then on the basis of the analysis of location precise, this paper presents the key technique and design points for experiment plat.

articleTitle: Ubiquitous MIMO radar energy integration detection based on range synthesis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: During such long-term time, the problem of target range-walk, Doppler-slide, beam-crossing must be considered, in the processing of the ubiquitous multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar energy integration detection. Commonly, keystone transform is adopted for the completion of the migration compensation, and then the integration is finally carried out by motion target detection or joint time-frequency analysis, the result of energy integration is limited to the migration compensation. An improved long-term energy integration method is proposed, it makes use of range synthesis for avoiding the processing of the migration compensation. The effectiveness of new method is conformed by the simulation results.

articleTitle: A novel range alignment method for ISAR imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In the Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) imaging process, the range alignment is the base of motion compensation and image reconstruction. The time difference between two consecutive radar echoes is very small, so the envelopes of two consecutive range images we get from two consecutive radar echoes are nearly the same. When two consecutive range images are aligned, their envelopes have the smallest difference, thus, the sum of squares of differences of corresponding range units of two consecutive range images is the least. Base on this theory, a new method of range alignment is proposed in this paper, which is called as the least variance method. The comparison between the least variance method and the minimum entropy method on the simulated and measured data processing demonstrates the effectiveness and superiority of the new method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Comparison of two detection-based adaptive variable update rate algorithms for tracking targets with phased array radars
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The effects of incorporating two kinds of detectors, the fading memory average of the acceleration (FMAA) and the fading memory average of the innovation (FMAI), into adaptive variable update rate algorithm for tracking targets are investigated and compared. Effective windows are used in the beginning and end of the maneuver to make a decision how to adaptively change the sampling interval. Simulation results show that the FMAA makes a better reflection of the maneuver compared with FMAI to get smaller errors in target tracking.

articleTitle: Digital array antenna measurement and azimuth accuracy analysis using real target's echoes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper provides an effective and easy to implement method for VHF digital array antenna measurement and system diagnostics under radar working situation. Using target's multiple channel echoes we can get perfect sum and different beam patterns through MTI and DBF processing. Azimuth accuracy was given by compare radar track positions with GPS values.

articleTitle: Research on characteristics of cylinder tanks in SAR image
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Cylinder tanks appear as arcs in SAR image. It is found the radius of some arcs is bigger than the radius of the tank. To analysis this phenomenon, combining the scattering theory and the principle of SAR, a novel prediction model about the SAR image of cylinder tanks, including the tanks with fixed top and floating top, is proposed. Analysis on details of the SAR image of the tanks is provided by the prediction model. Several experiments are implemented.

articleTitle: A cross-range scaling algorithm for range instantaneous doppler ISAR imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An instantaneous rotation rate (IRR) estimation algorithm based on the chirp rate of the scattering centre in the same Doppler cell is proposed to complete the cross-range scaling of the RID ISAR images.

articleTitle: Airborne MIMO radar clutter rank estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Range sidelobes increase the clutter subspace so that clutter rank is significantly higher than the rank of an idealized orthogonal waveform set. A rigorous proof is provided. Simulation results verified the conclusion.

articleTitle: InSAR interferometric phase estimation based on correlation weight subspace projection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper we propose a method to estimate the InSAR interferometric phase using the correlation weight subspace projection technique. In the method the correlation weight data vector is constructed, thus the noise subspace dimension of the corresponding covariance matrix will not be affected by the coregistration error, then avoiding the trouble of calculating the noise subspace dimension before estimating the InSAR interferometric phase. The method can auto-coregister the SAR images and reduce the interferometric phase noise simultaneously. The effectiveness of the method is verified via simulated data.

articleTitle: Airborne AESA radar's ECCM and self-defense jamming analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The peculiar character of flexible beam control and advanced waveform design of Active Electronically Steered Array (AESA) system brings powerful ECCM (Electronic Counter-Counter Measures) ability for airborne fire-control radar. This paper introduced all kinds of ECCM of airborne AESA radar first, especially for Low Probability of Intercept (LPI) technique and Space-Time Adaptive Processing (STAP) technique, then, it explored self-defense jamming approaches of combat aircraft in modern aerial warfare.

articleTitle: Relevance of the Hölderian regularity-based interpolation for range-Doppler ISAR image post-processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In ISAR processing, post-processing of the range Doppler image is useful to help the practitioner for ship recognition. Among the image post-processing tools, interpolation methods can be of interest especially when zooming. In this paper, we study the relevance of the Hölderian regularity-based interpolation. In that case, interpolating consists in adding a new scale in the wavelet transform and the new wavelet coefficients can be estimated from others. In the original method, initially proposed by two of the authors, the image is first interpolated along the rows and then along the columns. Concerning the diagonal pixels, they are estimated as the mean of the adjacent original and interpolated pixels. Here, we propose a variant where the diagonal pixels are estimated by taking into account the local orientation of the image. It has the advantage of conserving local regularity on all interpolated pixels of the image. A comparative study on synthetic data and real range-Doppler images is then carried out with alternative interpolation techniques such as the linear interpolation, the bicubic one, the nearest neighbour interpolation, etc. The simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Radar imaging simulation for typical urban structures based on analytical models
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper proposes a novel radar imaging simulator based on analytical electromagnetic and geometric models for a common typical kind of urban structure. The analytical models are presented not only for improving the efficiency of the simulation but also for direct and further understanding the features in the SAR image.

articleTitle: A S-band 50MW microwave amplifier's design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The S-band 50MW microwave amplifier is developed for National Synchrotron Radiation Laboratory (NSRL). This paper describes the design process of the amplifier and analyses the engineering realization of the pulse modulator. In the end, the running result of the amplifier is present.

articleTitle: Optimizing thinned antenna array geometry in MIMO radar systems using multiple genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To optimize thinned array pattern synthesis in multi-input multi-output radar, the distance perturbation is introduced and both transmit and receive antennas geometries are modified synchronously. Accordingly, pattern synthesis with a lower relative sidelobe level and maximum degrees of freedom are achieved.

articleTitle: Detection background segmentation and statistical analysis for High Frequency Surface Wave Radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A scheme of detection background segmentation and statistical analysis for High Frequency Surface Wave Radar (HFSWR) is presented. Clutter and noise in HFSWR is multi-sourced of which statistical distribution is complex. To overcome this problem, a detection background segmentation algorithm based on the cloud model is proposed to divide the background into several clutter/noise regions, and Weibull distribution is used to fit the segmentation regions, noted as seg-regions. According to the statistical fitting results, the difference of seg-regions is measured by KL divergence, and the segmentation algorithm is optimized.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of the radar signature of a new type of wind turbine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We present the results of measurements of the radar signature of a new type of wind turbine, named the Wind Lens. This design includes a shroud around the turbine which concentrates the wind flow past the turbine blades and hence improves the efficiency. The design also offers improved safety, and reduces acoustic noise. Furthermore, it may offer a significantly lower radar signature, which may make the design much more attractive for use in situations where conventional wind turbine designs may disturb the operation of radars in an unacceptable manner.

articleTitle: Azimuth multi-channel spotlight SAR imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Due to a system-inherent limitation, conventional SAR system is not capable of fulfilling the increasing demands of improved spatial resolution and wider swath coverage. Multi-channel SAR system is of great potential to realize high resolution wide swath (HRWS) imaging. This paper focuses on strategies to extend mapping extension of multi-channel SAR operated in spotlight mode. Subaperture based and modified deramping based approaches are put forward to implementing azimuth processing respectively.

articleTitle: Combined analysis of time&frequency synchronization error for BiSAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Signal model has great significance to time and phase synchronization research in a bistatic radar. In prevenient research, time synchronization and phase synchronization are investigated separately and their coupling relation has not been investigated. This paper introduces a bistatic radar signal model according to system's composition and operation procedure. From the radar operation principle, origin of time and phase synchronization in bistatic radar is revealed and their coupling relation is derived in theory.

articleTitle: Improving phase unwrapping techniques by the use of nonlinear phase model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a new efficient phase unwrapping algorithm for interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) phase images based on nonlinear phase model. Firstly, based on the analysis of statistical properties and signal characteristics of the interferometric phase, the concept of nonlinear phase model is proposed. It uses the nonlinear phase model of reflecting the topographic outline to approximate the interferometric phase change appeared in the local window. The lower amplitude bound of principal vector is defined and its value acquire method be given, which can effectively and adaptively extract the nonlinear components of the phase. Secondly, the nonlinear phase model is introduced to phase unwrapping, which increased the reliability of integration path and the accuracy of phase gradient, and improved effectively the performance of phase unwrapping. Real data processing results demonstrate the validity of the proposed nonlinear phase model and its corresponding processing method.

articleTitle: The X-band sub-array building block for active scalable array antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents an X-band multifunction, wideband and wide-angle scan sub-array building block (SBB) used in active scalable array antenna (ASAA). The configuration and development of the SBB and its key components are introduced in detail. The SBB has excellence extensibility of performance and structure, can be a fundamental radar element of scalable phased-array radar architecture to construct ASAA of varying size.

articleTitle: Research on fusion identification of aerial target based on kinematic state and foe-friend attribute
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In order to solve the problems of uncertainty and targets' time variation in the identification friend or foe, an algorithm which combines fuzzy reasoning, multi-level fuzzy comprehensive evaluation and D-S is presented. The simulations prove the algorithm's validity.

articleTitle: Detection ability modeling of balloon-borne radar against cruise missile
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To precisely estimate missile detection capability of balloon-borne radar is a key issue in designing low-altitude radar network. Based on stochastic service theory, an M/D/C finite queuing model of searching process is established, and the definition and calculation of balloon-borne radar service time, missing alarm probability and missile queuing time is presented. Through the analysis of L-88 balloon-borne radar search process, model validity is proved, the relationship between missing alarm probability and missile attack intensity is obtained. This model shows a good expansibility, and the results can be effectively applied to design land-based or air-based radar detection system.

articleTitle: Active phased antenna subarray module development for X-band SAR applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a block of active phased antenna subarray module was designed, simulated, fabricated and measured. Firstly, the topology of the active subarray module was described in detail. Then, six subassemblies of the module were designed, fabricated, test and optimised separately. At last, all subassemblies were assembled to form the whole module. Good measured results of the module validated that the design method was well fit for relative program.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a lightweight SAR transceiver subsystem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A lightweight Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) transceiver subsystem is presented in detail. Frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) transmitting and de-chirped receiving mode has been adopted in the system. Direct readout digital waveforms which can acquire the predistortion compensation, analog de-chirp and digital modulation techniques have also been used. The whole system consists of a CW transmitter, a single channel de-chirped receiver and an anti-vibration PLL frequency synthesizer. In addition, to solve the problem of miniaturization and EMC, the anti-vibration PLL synthesis technique has been brought into use. The transceiver system has some advantages of long pulse, low excitation power, broad bandwidth, and low sample rate. Presently, the system has been designed and fabricated, of which the weight is 800g; power consumption is about 40W and corresponding experiments have also been carried out. 0.5×0.5m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of maximum resolution has been obtained with the coverage of 8 km.

articleTitle: Improving the reliability of radar T/R module with precise cleaning technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Because we adopt high precision microelectronic assembly technologies during the manufacturing of radar T/R modules, these modules are complex and delicate. Common cleaning technologies such as ultrasonic cleaning can't satisfy the requirement of high precision cleaning of these modules. This article introduces some precise cleaning technologies, these cleaning technologies not only can make T/R module achieve a high cleanness, but also does little harm to them, and they will greatly improve the reliability of T/R module.

articleTitle: Wave model based enhancement of SAR ocean images
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Enhanced SAR ocean images with dominant wave-like signatures might promote oceanographic applications. Therefore we develop a wave model based processor for wave features enhancement. Algorithm analysis and experiments based on spaceborne (ERS-2) SAR ocean image show the reasonable capabilities.

articleTitle: A novel SAR imaging algorithm based on FrFT and CS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) radiates the chirps in the range direction, and their echoes also have the features of the chirp in the azimuth direction, so a novel imaging algorithm based on the fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) and the chirp scaling (CS) operation was proposed. The algorithm applied the CS operation to eliminate the space-variant of the range cell migration, and utilized the frequency-shift and compression properties of the FrFT to perform the bulk range cell migration correction and the range compression. After the FrFT on the azimuth direction, the target image in two-dimensional fractional Fourier domain was obtained. This algorithm may focus the target image described by two-dimensional impulse function only through one FFT and two FrFTs, hence its computational efficiency is improved significantly, which is superior to that of the classical CS algorithm and FrCSA.

articleTitle: Target initiation of high frequency surface wave Over-the-Horizon Radar based on information entropy theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The information from the high frequency surface wave Over-the-Horizon Radar includes range, angle, and radial velocity. Because the statistic information of angle measurement error is stable, with the range of target increase, the statistic error of tangential position get bigger, either, so the conventional logic method on target initiation leads to unstable results. Based on the Bayes estimation theory, this paper converts the initiation problem into a process of information entropy change, that means, the initiation problem is not only judged by the points number that associated from beginning to end, but also the quality of the associated points. In the end, the validity of the new method is proved by real data.

articleTitle: Phase-coded interrupted continuous waveform for two HF radars sharing the same frequency
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Phase-coded interrupted continuous waveform (PCICW) derived from P4 code is presented here for two radars sharing the same frequency. PCICW retains zero sidelobe within the range regions of interest. The transmitted codes from two radars are modulation multiplexed, and the echoes from different transmitters locate at different range regions after correlation computation. This waveform can improve the efficiency of frequency usage, and also make it possible to measure the total velocity through one receiver's outputs. A design example for two sea remote sensing HF ground wave radars (HFGWRs) is given here.

articleTitle: Range profile of extended target using frequency modulated stepped signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Traditional method directly do two times of pulse compressing to achieve the high resolution range profile of target illuminated by frequency modulated stepped signal. The method neglects the fact that the mainlobe of the first pulse compressing can be widen under the `tight restriction'. In this paper, the processing of the two times of pulse compressing is analyzed, and a method called `weighing the first pulse compressing' is proposed. The mothod can suppress the sidelobe of the first pulse compressing, and can make full use of the information of the echoes. The results of computer simulations are in agreement with the analysis of theories.

articleTitle: Study on the method of parameters analysis and scan mode of missile-borne SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper discusses how to design the scanning manner of antenna under the condition of steep dive and squint in missile-borne synthetic aperture radar (SAR). It proposes the uniform scanning method based on parameter fitting in the case of servo-mechanical control, and completes the analysis for resolution characteristics of the system in this mode. Meanwhile, the impact of the antenna scan on imaging is discussed and the analysis method of resolution under the condition of antenna scanning is obtained according to different imaging modes. The simulation example shows the effectiveness of the scanning method and can be applied to the practical engineering.

articleTitle: Modified direct data domain approach without space-time aperture loss
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We present herein a direct data domain approach without space-time aperture loss for airborne surveillance radar system. The approach is composed of three stages, i.e. reduced-resolution angle-Doppler image formation, full-dimension clutter subspace re-conformation and subspace projection. Simulation results confirm that the performance improvement achieved even secondary data-free, a feature that is particularly attractive for applications in heterogeneous environments.

articleTitle: Research on air target classification based on extraction of physical features of high-resolution radar range profiles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This article presents a method for coarse classification of targets based on extraction of size features of the one-dimensional high-resolution radar range profiles (HRRP). It analyzes the factors for limitation of the classification accuracy and puts forward the methods for improvement of classification accuracy and signal-noise ratio by means of movement compensation and integration on range profiles. The methods have been proven to be practically useful for coarse target classification by way of collection, analysis and verification of the data of four kinds of civil aviation air planes.

articleTitle: PolSAR image classification based on deorientation theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The randomly distributed target orientation causes confusion in classification of the polarimetric scattering target. In this paper, we proposed an unsupervised classification method to the fully polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) image to solve this problem. Firstly, we make a certain angle rotation of this part along the sight line to minimize the cross-polarized scattering; then we make an initial classification using the scattering mechanism described by the parameters; finally, using the initial classification result, the PolSAR image is classified by the modified C-mean algorithm. Experiment is performed on the real measured data; the result shows the proposed method is effective. u/v/H

articleTitle: Time-frequency quasi-matched intelligence receiver to LPI radar signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An intelligence receiver quasi-matched to the received LPI radar signals in time and frequency domain is presented. The architecture and prototype using FPGA and DSP are shown. The presented receiver works especially well when the received signals are complex and time-varying.

articleTitle: Study on sparse microwave imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Sparse signal processing is introduced to microwave imaging technology, which forms a new theory, new system and new methodology in microwave imaging. Defined as sparse microwave imaging, it means that by the sparse domain representation of the observed object, the sparse microwave signal is acquired by sparse sampling in space or time domain. After the signal processing and information extraction, the geometrical and physical characteristics of the observed object can be acquired with lower data rate and less hardware complexity of the imaging radar.

articleTitle: A method to estimate subspace via Doppler for ocean clutter suppression in skywave radars
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To detect ship targets within short coherent integration time (CIT), the ocean clutter suppressing technique has been used in high frequency (HF) skywave over-the-horizon-radar (OTHR). The clutter cancellation methods in time field are affected by estimate precision of frequency, amplitude and phase. The methods based on subspace are limited by the difficulty in determining the order of clutter subspace, and its performance degrades when the Doppler of target approximates to that of clutter. In this paper, the characteristics of both classes method are considered, and taking advantage of equivalence between clutter eigensubspace and subspace spanned by clutter Doppler frequency vectors, a novel method to estimate subspace via Doppler(ESVID) frequency for ocean clutter suppression in HF skywave radars is proposed, based on which ocean clutter is suppressed without eigen-decomposition. For ESVID method, apriori knowledge about Doppler frequency can be fully used, and only the frequency, without the amplitude and phase, need to be estimated. Finally, tests prove that, when a target appears closely to the clutter in Doppler domain, the ESVID method provides a signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) improvement of SCR about 10.5dB, 8.5dB and 6.5dB, compared with SVD, CC-FFT and EVD method, respectively.

articleTitle: A Track-Before-Detect Algorithm based on Particle Smoothing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An improved Track-Before-Detect Algorithm based on Particle Smoothing (PS-TBD) is proposed, with the consideration of the computation resources. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can improve effectively the target state estimation precision within a short time.

articleTitle: A new STAP method for MIMO radar based on joint digital beam forming and joint domain localized processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar has drawn unprecedented attention and becomes a main focus of research in the radar field. In this paper, we develop a novel STAP scheme for MIMO radar. The scheme takes advantage of the signals extracted by the matched filter (MF) bank which cascades with each receiver antenna element and forms a group of joint transmit-receive beams. A general sidelobe canceller (GSC) is derived to implement the adaptive matched filter (AMF) CFAR detection by employing a data level multistage wiener filter (DMWF) algorithm. This scheme reverses the unavailability of the phased-array-efficient joint-domain localized (JDL) algorithm for MIMO radar. Moreover, it adapts to MIMO radar with arbitrary ratio between transmitter and receiver element space. Even better, it needs less computed amount. We evaluate the validity of algorithm in terms of comparing the probability of detection performance and improving factor (IF) between phased array (PA) and MIMO radar.

articleTitle: Detection technique of the targets buried in blind doppler zone based on multi-AEW radar data fusion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Based on deliberate analysis of the detection problem concerning the target buried in blind Doppler zone of AEW radar, a target detection system is conceived founding on multi-AEW radar data fusion. The fusion rule as well as the generalized likelihood ratio and the false alarm threshold of local radar sensors are derived. Simulation results demonstrate that the advanced technique can improve the probability of target detection and the quality of target track dramatically in case the necessary condition is satisfied.

articleTitle: Improved STAP GMTI algorithm and its analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The FRACTA algorithm and its enhancements has been shown to be an effective STAP methodology for the airbore or spaceborne radar configuration in which there exists nonhomogenous clutter, jammer, and dense target clusters. But the FRACTA algorithm is rather complicated and has higher computational requirements, and can't estimate the target parameter accurately. In order to overcome the defects and adopt its advantages, the improved FRACTA algorithm is proposed, which can detect the targets and estimate the targets parameter accurately, and has higher efficient and robust than FRACTA. Simulation results indicate that improved algorithm overcomes the defects and inherits advantages commendably.

articleTitle: The imaging method of airborne radar on hybrid sampling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper introduces a high resolution imaging method, which is based on hybrid sampling of the airborne MIMO radar, combined the single snapshot of MIMO radar with the synthetic aperture of SAR. The method represents an equivalent array algorithm that the PRF of the system can be reduced dramatically to the conventional SAR, such that large unambiguity areas we can get. Numerical simulations are provided to examine the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Ground moving targets detection and relocation in heterogeneous environment for airborne radar based on tri-channel real data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper describes an approach for ground moving targets detection and relocation in heterogeneous environment which requires three consecutive operations as follows: Firstly, some deleterious factors correction techniques are adopted before clutter rejection. Secondly, different window selection strategies, aiming at different image coregistration error, are given to form the joint data vector for clutter rejection. Finally, the true target steering vector is derived in the presence of image coregistration error and channel mismatch, based on which the radial velocities of moving targets can be determined. Results of measured data processing are included to verify the robustness of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Application and molding technique research of Aramid fiber composites in radar components
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The paper detailedly introduced the mechanical, thermal and electromagnetic properties of Aramid fiber composites. The applications of Aramid fiber composites in radar components home and abroad were analysed. According to research and design requirements, resin transfered molding (RTM) technique was selected. Exploratory research was described from selection and technological test of resin system, establishment and control of technological parameters in molding process. Also the quality and performance of the products were detected, tested and appraised. The result shows that the quality and performance of final products are excellent and can meet the design and application requirements.

articleTitle: Multidimensional waveform design for multi-mode and synthetic bandwidth SAR imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To achieve multi-mode simultaneously for space -based radar, a multidimensional waveform in which the stepped frequency chirp signal is used among sub-pulses and sub-apertures is introduced. Synthetic bandwidth SAR imaging is elaborated. Simulation results are showed to illustrate the method.

articleTitle: A motion compensation technique for stepped-frequency radar with phase slope analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: When a stepped-frequency radar is used to obtain the synthesized high resolution range profiles (HRRPs) of high speed space objects, accurate motion compensation must be conducted, as object motion severely distorts the synthetic HRRPs. A novel method for estimating the motion parameters of a moving object from its stepped-frequency radar returns is presented. Motion parameters can be determined by analyzing the slope of the unwrapped phase function of the received radar signals. This method uses the maximum likelihood phase gradient estimation to calculate the phase slope of the radar signatures. Least squares estimation is incorporated into the phase slope analysis to reduce estimation errors. Numerical results show that the motion parameters can be accurately estimated and the HRRP distortion can be corrected.

articleTitle: Design of digital 2DOF servo system of shipboard tracking radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: All-digital servo system of shipboard tracking radar based on 2DOF (two degrees of freedom) system theory is designed in the paper. The paper puts forward a method of obtaining the feedforward controller of the two degrees of freedom system based on the step response curve of one degree of freedom system. The mathematical model of the servo system is established using MATLAB/Simulink, the two degrees of freedom velocity loop is designed, and the simulation results show that two degrees of freedom controller structure has significant role of enhancing the dynamic performance of the velocity loop, sensitivity function analysis verifies the robustness of the velocity loop. The hardware and software design of the servo system are Completed based on TMS320F28335 DSP, FOG (Fiber Optic Gyroscope) serves as inertial angular rate sensor of the velocity loop, the digital current loop is realized. Isolation experiment and tracking simulated moving target experiment are carried out, the experimental results show that the servo system has good dynamic performance and good disturbance attenuation capability.

Author Keywords: two degrees of freedom velocity loop

articleTitle: The influence factors analysis on the steering performances of liquid crystal optical phased array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The comprehensive analysis of several typical factors affecting the steering performance of LCOPA is made in this paper, the non-uniformity of lead resistance affecting the steering performance is first proposed, and the optimization method are conducted based on analysis results.

articleTitle: Research of time delay estimation methods in non-cooperative bistatic radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The main topic of this paper is cross-correlation detection and time delay estimation methods for fixed targets in non-cooperative bistatic radar systems. A time delay estimation method based on segment correlation - video integration is proposed to solve the problem of doppler mismatched loss for moving targets. Simulation results show that weak moving target can be detected and time delay can be fast estimated by segment correlation - video integration method, even when the difference of the signal-noise ratio of the reference channel and target channel is very great.

articleTitle: Improved three-stage inversion process for forest height inversion with PolInSAR data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Three-stage inversion process is one of the most frequently used methods with PolInSAR data for extracting forest heights. According to this method, forest heights and ground topography can be extracted based on interferometric coherence using a random volume over ground model. In this paper, a coherence value estimation method with adaptive averaging window derived from coherence region shape parameters is presented to improve the accuracy of complex coherence estimate. Moreover, coherence region boundary extraction algorithm is applied to resolve the ambiguity estimation problem of volume decorrelation. Finally, the proposed algorithm is validated by simulated PolInSAR data for canopy simulated by PolInSAR data simulator of PolSARpro software developed by ESA (European Space Agency).

articleTitle: Necessary study on Airborne Radar Network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Airborne Radar Network has the advantage over Airborne Single Radar in three aspects. Firstly how does it have the performance of countering stealth airplane and of hiding itself; Secondly how does it shorten the time of detecting object; Lastly how does it improve the recognized precision and positioned precision of object.

articleTitle: Sequential waveforms optimization for wideband target recognition radar based on kernel method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Aiming at the problem of sequential waveform design for radar target recognition with imprecise prior knowledge, a kernel based sequential waveform design algorithm inspired by power transformed correlation kernel is proposed. Numerical results show the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: The research of amplitude statistical distribution of terrain return in vertical incidence region
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper describes the experiment of measurement of terrain return in the vertical incidence region by 8mm, S-band radar scatterometer. Then using Rank Sum Test, this paper verifies the statistics properties of the amplitude distribution of terrain return in vertical incidence region. It concluded that the distribution is Rayleigh distribution, and it is affected by the terrain roughness and radar wavelength.

articleTitle: A digital compensation technique to the aperture effect of the stepped Chirp wideband phased array radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To apply the stepped chirp signal to the actual wideband phase arrayed radar system, the ghosts on the range profile when wide-angle scanning, must be solved. First the ghosts, which emerge since the aperture effect for the stepped Chirp wideband phased array radar, are traversed, both the position and the amplitude of the ghosts are calculated in this paper, and then a digital compensation method is presented to minimize the ghost. Simulation result indicates that the proposed method can suppress the ghosts effectively.

articleTitle: A target reference template generation method for image matching guidance with missile-borne SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Target reference template generation is a key technique for radar image matching guidance. The generation method selection mostly determines the overall performance of radar image matching guidance system. In this paper, a method of target reference template generation for image matching guidance with missile-borne SAR based on echo signal simulation of missile-borne SAR is presented. The feasibility and the effectiveness of the generation method are proved.

articleTitle: A novel two-dimensional frequency spectrum for bistatic SAR processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The frequency spectrum expression plays a key role in bistatic SAR image formation. However, due to the existence of double-square-roots in the bistatic range equation, it is difficult to obtain an analytical two-dimensional spectrum. This paper derives a novel spectrum expression for bistatic SAR processing. Based on the appropriate approximation, the original range equation with double-square-roots form can be approximated as the sum of a linear function and a single square-root. Thus the analytical stationary point and spectrum expression can be calculated according the principle of stationary phase. Finally, numerical simulations are performed to validate the proposed frequency spectrum.

articleTitle: An improved combined interacting multiple models probabilistic data association algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Considering the impact of the common measurements for updating the track to improve PDA algorithm, an improved combined interacting multiple models probability data association(IC-IMMPDA) algorithm, combining IMM algorithm with improved PDA algorithm is proposed. The simulation's results show that the new algorithm is not only much better than the combined interacting multiple models probabilistic data association (C-IMMPDA) algorithm, but also keeping small calculation cost in the environment of dense targets.

articleTitle: An improved unsupervised threshold determination method for SAR image change detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: One of the key techniques for multi-temporal synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image change detection is how to select and determine the threshold. The Kittler and Illingworth (KI) algorithm is an unsupervised threshold determined method based on the least error ratio of the Bayesian theory. Although it is a simple and feasible parameter estimation approach, there are some deficiencies. In order to improve these deficiencies, this paper proposes an improved unsupervised threshold determination method on the basis of the KI algorithm, and it is called mean circulation iteration KI (MCI-KI) algorithm. The main idea of the MCI-KI algorithm is to shorten the scope of selecting the threshold via controlling errors. So it reduces the burden of computation and saves the running time. Finally, the airborne and spaceborne SAR images are used to test the proposed method, and experimental results verify that the method is effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Target localization for bistatic MIMO radar in unknown correlated noise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, target localization for bistatic MIMO radar in unknown spatially correlated noise is investigated. In our model, both the transmitter and receiver arrays are divided into two subarrays. A novel target localization algorithm is proposed by jointly estimating the directions-of-departure (DODs) and directions-of-arrival (DOAs) for transmitter and receiver subarrays in unknown noise. The algorithm exploits the canonical correlation decomposition (CCD) and the joint estimation technology based on the shift-invariance properties of different subarrays obtaining the automatic pairing. In addition, the compact formulas of stochastic Cramer-Rao bounds (CRB's) for DOD and DOA estimation are derived. The simulations show that our method effectively improves the performance of estimation by eliminating the unknown correlated noise.

articleTitle: Adaptive generalized DPCA algorithm for clutter suppression in airborne radar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an adaptive generalized displaced phased center antenna (AGDPCA) algorithm for clutter suppression in airborne radar from a viewpoint of a two-dimensional pulse-to-pulse canceller. First, the clutter model and signal model are given in matrix-vector form, and this leads naturally to the design of a two-dimensional (2-D) two-pulse (2-P) canceller and the GDPCA algorithm formulation. Second, the AGDPCA algorithm is developed by dynamically estimating the 2-D 2-P canceller from the received data. Third, the 2-D 2-P canceller is extended to 2-D multi-pulse canceller to improve the moving target detection performance in AGDPCA algorithm. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is tested via several experiments.

articleTitle: The ballistic missile tracking method using dynamic model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Ballistic missile tracking in time is one of the key technologies in the missile defence system. Aiming at problems about ballistic missile kinetic states real-time estimation, this paper investigated the method of ballistic missile tracking using dynamic model. Firstly, based on analyzing characteristics of ballistic missile's motion, this paper builds dynamics model of ballistic missile under the condition of gravity turn model; Secondly, based on analyzing parameter of dynamic model, this paper builds simplified kinetic model of ballistic missile; Lastly, this paper analyses how to chose kinetic states variable, and then educes ballistic missile kinetic states function and simulates the method of real-time estimation based on EKF, the result shows that the proposed method can track the ballistic missile, what is more, the estimation precision is high.

articleTitle: Super-resolution ISAR imaging via statistical compressive sensing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Developing compressed sensing (CS) theory has been applied in radar imaging by exploiting the inherent sparsity of radar signal. In this paper, we develop a super resolution (SR) algorithm for formatting inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image with limited pulses. Assuming that the target scattering field follows an identical Laplace probability distribution, the approach converts the SR imaging into a sparsity-driven optimization in Bayesian statistics sense. We also show that improved performance is achieved by taking advantage of the meaningful spatial structure of the scattering field. To well discriminate scattering centers from noise, we use the non-identical Laplace distribution with small scale on signal components and large on noise. A local maximum likelihood estimator combining with bandwidth extrapolation technique is developed to estimate the statistical parameters. Experimental results present advantages of the proposal over conventional imaging methods.

articleTitle: Research on pre-processing method of motion compensation for forward-looking SAR imaging based on navigational data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In order to solve the platform balleting effect on the forward-looking SAR focusing imaging, a new pre-processing algorithm based on navigational data is proposed. The proposed algorithm establishes a new coordinate transform to convert the WGS-84 ellipsoidal coordinate measured by the navigational equipments to the local space Cartesian coordinate, which people used to apply in SAR imaging. At the same time, the two-step delay method based on self-installed registration point is applied to get the precise platform air data to realize exact movement compensation for forward-looking imaging. Simulation indicates that the proposed algorithm can improve the performance of platform imaging system.

articleTitle: Design of radar ECCM performance testing system and its semi-physical simulation experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper describes the theory, design, implementation, simulation and testing of a radar ECCM performance testing system capable of generating target echo, clutter and jamming signal for radar ECM/ECCM experiment. With the help of the proposed testing system, the jamming styles and parameters can be smartly intercalated with a variety of simulation scenarios. The rubs are resolved such as radar states data acquisition, echo real time simulation and display & control terminals setup of signal environment. Then a radar ECM semi-physical simulation experiment is applied to measure six typical ECCM performance indexes in the signal environment generated by the testing system. Experiment and data processing results show the testing platform is valid and practical. The testing system can be used to solve problems such as radar ECCM performance evaluation, radar advanced design and ECCM strategies when the equipment is relatively small in tracking and guidance phase.

articleTitle: Sum and difference Doppler filter banks canceller for GMTI in airborne radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A sum and difference Doppler filter banks canceller is introduced as a novel temporal adaptive processor. In this canceller, sum and difference Doppler filter banks are artificially formed to complete clutter cancellation for the tested Doppler channel, and improved clutter suppression and slow moving target detection performance can be achieved. The canceller also provides a remarkable computationally efficient means by temporal adaptive processing with sum and difference Doppler filters. In addition, results are shown for a high-fidelity, simulated clutter environment and a real clutter data of airborne fire control radar. The results indicate the presented canceller produces a marked SCNR performance improvement over conventional methods.

articleTitle: ISAR imaging based on antenna array and compressed sensing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Compressed sensing (CS) has recently attracted much interest for its ability to recovery a sparse signal with very limited number of samples. In this paper, we adapt this idea and present a framework of high-resolution ISAR imaging based on antenna array. During the framework, linear antenna array is analyzed and compared with different conventional algorithms. Numerical simulation results confirmed the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Real-time beam position design for high-dynamic platform SAR system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Unconstant velocity and nonlinear movement are two characteristics of high-dynamic SAR platform. With respect to the uncertainty of the parameters, in this paper, a real-time approach for designing beam position is proposed. Furthermore, the simulation for system design is given. And the approach is evaluated by the results of simulation.

articleTitle: Forward looking SAR imaging algorithm via CS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Forward-looking SAR is a system that is imaging for the frontal targets of the flight path. The forward looking SAR designed by DLR employs linear antenna array. The imaging resolution is limited by the short synthetic aperture which results from the short antenna. This paper presents a F-SAR imaging algorithm based on compressive sensing, which achieves higher imaging resolution in the same case with the system of DLR. This algorithm constructs the filter functions in the time domain which are independent of the target number and Doppler frequency. The effectiveness of the scheme is revealed through simulation results.

articleTitle: Cyclostationary detector in ultra Wideband Impulse Radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we provide a new approach in ultra Wideband (UWB) radars based on a Fourier series with time-varying coefficients resulting in a second-order cyclostationary characteristics for stationary (low-mobility) target and almost second-order cyclostationary characteristics in moving target scenario. We also provide a new method for blind detection based on detecting the presence of cyclostationarity. The new MMSE estimator is based on the unconditional orthonormal signal representation for almost cyclostationary characteristics, moreover, based on this estimation, a new method for detection of UWB radar signals in presence of (non)-Gaussian additive noise in stationary and moving target scenario is provided. We utilize the discrete prolate spheroidal sequences (DPSS) as the unconditional orthonormal signals. The purposed methods require no a priori information, except the pulse repetition interval, to detect signal of interest. Simulations for CFAR detectors are presented to compare the introduced new method with cyclostationary detector and the conventional UWB radar detectors called interleaved periodic correlation processing (IPCP).

articleTitle: Integration detection research for high-speed and small target
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Aiming at range migration in integration detection for high-speed and small target, the paper adopts parameter estimation and compensation in target detection. When estimating the target parameter, a new method of unambiguous Doppler frequency estimation is proposed, which resolves the problem of Doppler ambiguity, avoids the estimation of fuzzy factor, reduces the calculation quantity and lowers the demand of the input SNR at meantime. It is suitable for multi-target circumstance. Then, using of the estimated frequency of Doppler, the echo signal phase is compensated, without the influence of range migration. So this method can improve the detection performance of high-speed and small target greatly.

articleTitle: Attitude control accuracy allocation for the Spaceborne SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The problem of attitude control accuracy for Spaceborne SAR is examined based on the error theory. According to the relationship between Doppler parameters and spacecraft attitude, a method of attitude control accuracy allocation is proposed and validated with the simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of micro-Doppler signatures of moving vehicles by using empirical mode decomposition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper utilizes empirical mode decomposition to analyze the micro-motion of moving vehicles. Due to the adaptive function of empirical mode decomposition (EMD), different micro-motion of moving vehicles can be extracted by this decomposition technique. The analysis results based on simulated data and measured data show that special structures of different vehicles can be well depicted by EMD.

articleTitle: Scatterers integrator based on the maximum variance of order statistics in non-Gaussian clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To improve the robustness of modified scatterer density dependent (MSDD) detector, a scatterers integrator based on the maximum variance of order statistics (SI-MVOS) is proposed. Firstly, the number of scatterers of target is estimated based on the maximum variance of order statistics. Secondly, the energy of estimated scatterers is integrated to form the detection statistic. Its detection performance is analyzed, results show that the SI-MVOS estimates the number of scatterers adaptively according to the observations, and it can improve performance and robustness of detector effectively.

articleTitle: 3D bistatic imaging geometry applied to near range microwave system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Near range microwave imaging techniques have broad application prospects in the field of concealed weapon detection, biomedical imaging, non-destructive testing, etc. In this paper, the 3D bistatic imaging geometry based on planar scanning aperture are proposed to be applied to near range microwave imaging, which can obtain the bistatic reflectivity of targets and consequently conduce to classify and identify different targets; Then, this paper establishes the echo model in this imaging geometry, and deduces the 3D bistatic Omega-K imaging algorithm based on the Loffeld's bistatic formula (LBF) method; Finally, through numerical simulation, verifies the imaging geometry and imaging algorithm proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Scattering characteristic analysis and underwater acoustic measurement experiment for ship targets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, the multipath scattering characteristics is studied for ship targets nearby rough sea surface. Firstly, the sea-surface reflection is modeled by a specular component and a diffuse component. Based on the multipath model, the scattering intensity of radar target is analyzed for ship target nearby rough sea surface. Furthermore, the expression of the factor influence on the ship targets in the presence of sea-surface induced multipath is given with the radar equation. Lastly, with the comparability of the acoustic wave and the electromagnetic wave, the validity of the method proposed is proved by the results of the underwater acoustic measurement experiment.

articleTitle: Cognitive over-the-horizon radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Combined the characteristics of skywave over-the-horizon radar with the concept of cognitive radar, cognitive over-the-horizon radar (COTHR) becomes an important development approach of over-the-horizon radars. Integrating multitasking requirements with real-time dynamically sensing to propagation media--the ionosphere, COTHR assigns intelligently the missions and resources, achieves the best detection. In this paper, the definition of COTHR has been proposed firstly. And the characteristics of COTHR, including environment sensing, continuously iteration, and spectrum management, have been discussed in detail. Finally, some key techniques have been addressed.

articleTitle: A study on the application of millimeter-wavelength cloud radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In recent years, millimeter-wavelength radar plays an important role in radar remote sensing field. In this article, application of this technique is introduced at first. Then the observation of non-precipitating and weak precipitation clouds by this type of radar is compared with those obtained by X-Band weather radar. The comparison shows that millimeter-wavelength cloud radar is a better way in both the macroscopic and microscopic investigation of clouds. However, this technique undergoes serious rain attenuation which is also introduced in the article.

articleTitle: Orbit determination of multiple spatial targets based on space-borne phased array radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For the problem of far-near effect, a sum-difference multi-beamforming with null broadening and mainlobe keeping is proposed. With measurements of direction of arrivals and ranges, orbits of spatial targets are determinated by coordinate conversion, Laplace iteration and six parameters estimation. Simulation results demonstrate high precision of the method.

articleTitle: Spatial baseline decorrelation of geosynchronous circular SAR interferometry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: With appropriate orbit parameters, the circular SAR imaging mode can be realized on the geosynchronous orbit satellite to get high resolution three-dimensional (3D) image. It would also overcome the coverage and revisit period limitation. Repeat pass interferometry for geosynchronous circular SAR (GEOCSAR) could be carried out, comparing images taken at 24 hours interval. The geosynchronous orbit is influenced by perturbations, which cause the variation of the orbit and thus the spatial baseline is formed. The spatial baseline decorrelation of GEOCSAR interferometry in 2D and 3D model are analyzed, and the corresponding critical baselines are derived in this paper.

articleTitle: Ground clutter censoring for airborne weather radar employing DEM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A ground clutter rejection method based on Digital Elevation Model (DEM) is proposed, which can be used to censor the clutter when airborne weather radar operates in weather mode. The theory of visibility analysis is used to identify the ranges with clutter. The terrain altitude in DEM and the height of points at the line-of-sight is compared, and the ranges where the beam crosses the surface or mountain are identified. Then these ranges with clutter are edited and rejected, so the suppression is implemented directly in time domain. In virtue of the proposed algorithm, the ranges where the clutter exists can be computed accurately using radar parameters and DEM. Finally, the validity and effectivity of the presented method is verified by processing the measured airborne data.

articleTitle: Aperture effect influence and analysis of stepped frequency wideband phased array radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Wideband phased array has high range resolution. It can realize target recognition and radar imaging, which provides key technical support for modern high-performance radar meeting the future war demand. However, the aperture effect will cause the beam-pointing shift, broaden the main lobe of the one-dimension target range profile, lower the resolution, and reduce the signal to noise ratio (SNR). Each pulse in the standard stepped frequency waveform is a narrow band signal. It achieves the large instantaneous wideband by the synthesis of the pulse sequence. Therefore we can use interveinal phase matching to compensate the aperture effect.
