This paper analyzes the relationship between the wideband antenna beam-pointing with the instantaneous signal frequency, and introduces the principle of stepped frequency synthesis wideband, then simulates the method of interveinal phase matching, the simulation results show that this method can compensate the aperture effect of stepped frequency wideband phased array effectively, lastly get high resolution and high precision one-dimension target range profile.

articleTitle: Bi-Capon beamforming for MIMO radar: A correlation matrix-based method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a bi-Capon beamforming (BCB) algorithm for MIMO radar based on a simplified correlation matrix is investigated. By vectorising the received data matrix and its transpose and iteratively optimizing two lower dimensional weight vectors, the bi-Capon beamforming (BCB) method can significantly decrease the computational complexity and the training samples requirement. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: System characteristics of UWB Bistatic through-wall SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Bistatic through-wall imaging SAR has a promising future. A model of Bistatic SAR for through-wall sensing is established, whose transmitter working in side-looking strip mode with a stationary receiver. Aiming at the requirements of imaging algorithm development on system characteristics, the paper focuses on characteristics of Doppler, space dependence, and two dimensional (2-D) resolution distribution. Through theoretical derivation in time and frequency domain combined with simulation analysis, formulas of the characteristic indexes are obtained as well as the influence of system configuration and wall parameters on them. All these lay the theoretical foundation for the development of precise imaging algorithm.

articleTitle: Compact tapered slot antenna for wideband applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a compact exponentially tapered slot antenna (ETSA) with invert-L slots edge (ILSE) structure is presented. The proposed antenna is composed of a step-shaped transition from microstrip to slotline for feeding arrangement and a tapered patch with invert-L slots edge as radiation element. Compared to the conventional ETSA version, the proposed design skill of introducing ILSE at ground patch has the capability to extend the impedance bandwidth to lower band and improve the radiation characteristics at lower frequency bands.

articleTitle: Experimental system and results for wide-band multi-polarization VHF radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For synthetically utilizing frequency and polarization information to improve the abilities of radar detection and recognition, an experimental system with wide-band multi-polarization VHF radar is presented. And the field experimental results are introduced in detail.

articleTitle: Radar dynamic echo simulation of ship targets in terminal guidance based on quasi-static method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Radar dynamic echoes modeling and simulation are important prerequisites and groundwork for target detection and identification. Taking linear frequency modulation (LFM) terminal guidance radar as an example, we first analyze the time scale of the quasi-static method in echo simulation, and establish the dynamic echo simulation model of ship targets. The motion equations of missile and ship were given in a typical attacking scenario, and the target dynamic echoes during the whole attacking process were simulated. The simulation results show that echoes reflect the characteristics of target motion very well, which provide data support for the further research on radar target detection and recognition.

articleTitle: An improved method to sort and pair TDOA based on the correlation between TDOAs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In TDOA passive location system, the situations in which false TDOA combinations arose are sorted. For extracting the correct TDOA combination of the radiant source, an improved method to sort and pair TDOA is proposed in this paper. The method can eliminate the false TDOA combinations which are reduced by sub-PRI(pulse repetition interval) of the radiant source with high pulse repetition frequency(PRF) and the equality of multiple targets' TDOAs, and associate all TDOA combinations which belong to the same target. The method enhances the accuracy of extracting TDOA combination and reduces the computation load and the complexity of afterward processing.

articleTitle: Ground slow moving target's signal analysis for Interferoemtric SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Ground slow moving target detection using Interferoemtric SAR (InSAR) technique often omits the defocusing effect and just assumes that moving target has perfect Point Spread Function (PSF) as stationary point target does. In order to examine the defocusing effect on Interferometric Phase (IP) of moving target, we deduces the analytic description of moving target's PSF and the interferoemtric phase under Along-Track Interferometric (ATI) mode and hybrid Along- and Across-Track interferometric mode. The effectiveness of moving target's theoretical interferometric signal descriptions deduced is validated by simulations. Then, the clutter effects are also discussed and the interferoemtric signal modes of moving target plus clutter are also considered.

articleTitle: Radar target recognition based on some invariant properties of the polarization scattering matrix
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In order to meet the needs of radar target recognition (RTR), a method using some invariant properties of the polarization scattering matrix (IPPSM) is presented. A simulated cone model of missile is used to test in microwave darkroom experiments, a new IPPSM is first presented, its physical characteristic is also given. All the IPPSMs are analyzed, the experiment results imply that Determinant |Δ|, Trace of Power Scattering Matrix P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, Module of Polarization Ellipticity |τ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>|, Polarization Combination Coefficient η are invariant with the orientation angles. From the Depolation D, Polaization Ellipticity τ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, we know that the target has multi-scattering centers and is symmetric which are true for the real target, so a 7-dim polarization vector X=(|Δ|, P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, D, φ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, τ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, |τ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>|, η) can be usefully obtained for radar target recognition.

Author Keywords: invariant properties of the polarization scattering matrix (IPPSM)

articleTitle: Target detection algorithm for polarimetric SAR images using GOPCE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A new target detection algorithm based on the generalized optimization of contrast enhancement (GOPCE) is proposed in this paper. Using the measured POL-SAR data, we compare the performances of the new detector and several conventional detectors, showing the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An array calibration method using spatial correlation properties for HFSWR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper focuses on calibration of uniform linear array (ULA) for high frequency surface wave radar. A novel algorithm is proposed based on spatial correlation properties of the calibration source. We can estimate amplitude from the main diagonal elements of spatial correlation matrix, and obtain DOA (direction of arrival) estimate of the calibration source by two-dimension FFT. The spatial correlation matrix could be estimated in temporal domain and frequency domain, which performs better in low SNR case. It is shown through Monte Carlo simulations and experimental results that this method is practical and reliable.

articleTitle: Weak target detection based on the Membership Degree of the IMFs Energy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In the paper, the proportions of the sea clutter Intrinsic Mode Functions (ab. IMFs) energy to the whole signal energy and the influence of the target on the proportions are discussed. It is found that the latter low frequency IMFs are weaker when no target is hit, but they are stronger when the target is hit, and the proportions of their energy to the whole signal energy become larger, which could be described by the Membership Degree of the IMFs Energy (ab. MDIE). So the MDIE is proposed to detect the weak target, whose performance to detect the slowly fluctuant target in the sea clutter is better than the one of the weak target detection method directly using the box dimension.

articleTitle: Resistively loaded ultra-wideband dipole antenna for narrow borehole radar systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a resistive loading ultra-wideband (UWB) dipole antenna for narrow borehole radar systems with discrete Wu-King resistive profile, which is realized by loading lumped resistors discretely on both arms of the dipole antenna. The proposed antenna has many advantages for ground penetrating radar (GPR) applications such as reduced wire dipole diameter, less late-time ringing, and relatively high radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Multiple moving targets imaging for millimeter-wave InISAR based on time-frequency transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Time-frequency transform is applied into InISAR for multiple moving targets imaging. By means of interferometric processing to range-Doppler images, the range-azimuth image can be derived from the interferometric phase. The restriction of millimeter-wave (MMW) phase wrapping is solved by multiple baseline.

articleTitle: A novel SAR imaging algorithm based on compressed sensing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: High speed A/D sampling and large scale data storage are two basic challenges of the high resolution SAR system. The developing of radar system is limited by these two challenges under the Nyquist sampling theory. Compressed sensing (CS) is a new approach of sparse signals recovered beyond the constraints of Nyquist sampling technique. With the consideration of these problems that might happen and the advantage of CS theory, a novel SAR image processing algorithm based on compressive sensing was proposed in this paper. Using the data whose sampling rate is lower than the required Nyquist sampling rate, the CS-based algorithm operates at range and azimuth dimensional respectively. Experimental results show the presented algorithm based on compressed sensing have a better performance than the conventional SAR algorithm even with only smaller samples, and also indicate that the presented algorithm is robustness with existence of serious noise

articleTitle: An angle estimation algorithm for MIMO radar in the presence of colored noise fields
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An angle estimation method for Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar in the presence of colored noise fields is presented. In this method, the transmitter array is divided into two sub-arrays. Then a new correlation matrix can be constructed by the received data from two transmitter sub-arrays and reconstructed data. The influence of spatial colored noise can be eliminated by the cross correlation matrix and the angle can be estimated by ESPRIT-MUSIC. The parameters can be paired automatically and the angle estimation performance of the proposed method is better than other methods in low SNR. Simulation results are presented to verify the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: New nonparametric detectors under K-distributed sea clutter in radar applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Based on modified rank test, this paper proposes two new nonparametric detectors by using the K-distributed sea clutter model. These two detectors are Modified-Rank-based Generalized Sign detector (MRGS) and Modified-Rank-based Mann-Whitney detector (MRMW). The new detectors are achieved by designing the inverse-normal-score functions of the rank statistics. They are CFAR (Constant False Alarm Rate) for the data with continuous CDF (Cumulative Distribution Function) and with PDF (Probability Density Function) bing symmetric about zero. The performance of the new detectors is analyzed under the Swerling II target model by Monte-Carlo simulation. We compare the results of our proposed detectors with two classical nonparametric detectors: Generalized Sign (GS) detector and Mann-Whitney (MW) Detector. The most important conclusion is that the detectability of nonparametric detector is insensitive to the change of the scale parameter b but just depends on the shape parameter v of the K-distributed clutter for the Swerling II target model. Moreover, nonparametric detector especially for the proposed MRMW detector in this paper is quite suitable for low observable targets detection under spiky K-distributed sea clutter.

articleTitle: Segmentation process for SAR imagery based on graph cuts algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper proposes a method that comes from the minimum cut problem in network flow theory to minimize the MRF energy of posteriori probability. Then maximum flow or minimum cut algorithm is used to deal with MRF segmentation. Experiments on SAR images prove that the proposed method has better accuracy and faster efficiency than standard algorithms.

articleTitle: Detection and classification of radar false targets based on transmitted signal with random linear modulation frequency ratio
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Aiming to RLFMR signal, the CCCPF is used to measure the degree of similarity between the real target and the false one. Next, a GLRT detector is designed. The simulations are provided to evaluate the performance of this algorithm.

articleTitle: The 1000W microwave solid state power amplifier at Ku band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In order to satisfy the demand of power and frequency of the power amplifier in radar system, Power synthesis technology and method of microwave wide bandand solid state power amplifier (SSPA) is discussed in this paper. By calculating the influence of phase and amplitude difference on the power output of SSPA, The maximal allowable phase difference and amplitude difference in every power module is presented and the circuit topology is presented too. At last SSPA with 1000 watt power output and 20% bandwidth at Ku band is desiged.

articleTitle: Rescue radar's signal processing method based on Doppler features of phase structure an echo-signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In paper the targets selection method based on Doppler features of phase structure an echo-signal is considered. Sounding of the targets is carried out by a noise signal, providing high reserve and a noise stability of system. The idea of orthogonal decomposition of a signal and exact representation of function is put in a basis of a method on discrete set of points by full system of basic functions. The algorithm of calculation of spectral estimations on the sample of a signal limited in time is constructed. The algorithm allows to calculate spectral estimations quasiperiodical processes with characteristic frequencies from 0,1 up to 10 Hz. Stability and noise immunity of algorithm is investigated. It is shown, that unlike known methods of the spectral super resolution the offered method does not give false spectral when the signal/noise ratio decreased.

articleTitle: Collocated MIMO radar beamforming with two side adaptivity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We propose a beamforming algorithm for collocated multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with two side adaptivity capability such that more active and inactive interferences can be suppressed at a low computational complexity and a low sample number requirement. Signals only with jamming and noise signals are used as training samples to obtain the weighting vector for receiving beamforming. After receiving beamforming, signals that may contain targets of interest are range compressed and then pass the adaptive transmitting beamforming to suppress inactive interferences. Numerical experiments show that this algorithm can suppress more interferences than the MIMO Capon algorithm, at a lower computation cost than the MIMO two-side beamforming algorithm.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of signal processing algorithm for high altitude pulse compression radar altimeter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel signal processing algorithm design for an intra-pulse LFM (linear frequency modulation) & inter-pulse PPM (pulse position modulation) compression radar altimeter is given. In order to enhance the performance of signal processing algorithm, a correlation integration algorithm based on mismatched code is provided. The corresponding flight verification test results in different terrain have been presented. Flight test shows that the signal processing algorithm of the high altitude pulse compression radar altimeter has very high processing gain and superior performance for weak echo signal detection.

articleTitle: A super-resolution algorithm based on passive millimeter wave imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a super-resolution algorithm based on Lucy-Richardson acceleration algorithm is proposed for passive millimeter wave imaging. It is demonstrated by experiments the algorithm improves the convergence rate, enhances the resolution and is conductive to passive millimeter wave imaging.

articleTitle: Relationship between radar signatures and target motion modes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Aerial target motion modes have a close relationship with its attitude angles, hence with radar signatures. Expressions for radar signatures are derived from target echo signal firstly, including radar cross section (RCS) and angular glint error. A theoretical analysis on attitude rates of radar line-of-sight (LOS) under different motion modes is then performed. Taking a two-scatterer simple target as an example, we establish the relationship between radar signatures and the attitude rates of radar LOS. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical analysis. The conclusions are significant for feature-aided motion mode identification and maneuver detection technologies.

articleTitle: Analysis and extraction of micro-doppler features in FMCW-ISAR using a Modified Extended Hough Transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The micro-Doppler (m-D) features of targets based on the FMCW-ISAR is analysed in this paper. The influence of the Doppler frequency shift induced by the target's continuous moving in pulse repetition interval (PRI) is discussed, and then a method named Modified Extended Hough Transform is proposed to extract the parameters of m-D features from the spectrogram. The simulation experiment validates the theoretical conclusions in m-D features analysing, and m-D features extraction.

articleTitle: A new cross-range scaling method for ISAR based on the multiple dominant scatterers synthesis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of cross-range scaling of inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR). It is the basis of obtaining the information about the target, such as the size and the shape. To accomplish the cross-range scaling, the rotating velocity (RV) of the target needs to be estimated first. In this paper, a new approach is presented for estimating the RV by analyzing the relation between the chirp rate of the cross-range signal and the range cell. A technique based on the multiple dominant scatterers synthesis is used to estimate the chirp rate. Finally, real data processing results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed cross-range scaling method.

articleTitle: Life detection based on cross-correlation analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A life detection method based on cross-correlation analysis is proposed. It applies to a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) background. The experiment results with real data illustrate the theoretical validity.

articleTitle: Modernizing a radar with a digital receiver
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper describes how a radar is modernized with a digital receiver. The paper shows the methodology for this, including the characterization of the old analogue receiver and different aspects of the system design of the new digital receiver. The existing radar is modernized in an evolutionary process i.e. replace one or a few sub-units at a time with the latest technology. For the case in this paper the radar was modernized with a digital receiver. Several analogue units were replaced with two PCBs containing FPGAs. This gives higher reliability and lower Life Cycle Cost, reduces the obsolescence risk and, ensures an inherent flexibility in waveform design.

articleTitle: Analysis of mainlobe to mean square sidelobe ratio in noise radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, the mathematical expression of mainlobe to mean square sidelobe ratio (MMSSR) is deduced by analyzing the statistic properties of the output of the range/Doppler processing in noise radar. The main factors influencing MMSSR are investigated, including pulse compression length, discrete Fourier transform (DFT) length, Doppler frequency, signal to noise ratio (SNR) and the weighted window. The correctness of the conclusions has been verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Mobile sensor registration in ECEF coordinates using the MLR algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A new algorithm is presented to align multiple 3-D mobile sensors in the Earth-Centred-Earth-Fixed coordinate system, which is called MLMR algorithm for short. The MLMR algorithm can effectively estimate sensor biases, sensor frame orientation and target state. For illustrative purposes, the MLMR algorithm is applied to simulated track data from two 3-D sensors.

articleTitle: Moving target parameter estimation of spaceborne SAR-GMTI based on the analysis of acceleration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Aiming at the influence of fast moving target with acceleration in imaging and parameter estimation, a novel method for moving target detection and parameter estimation with three-channel is proposed. After the moving target echo is analyzed, the general two-order keystone transform is applied to eliminate range curve for clutter suppression result. Time-frequency analysis is employed to construct phase compensation function and correct the residual range walk. Finally, azimuth Fourier transform is performed to get the image. Moving target parameters can be obtained by the interferometric processing technology. Simulation results show the validity of the method.

articleTitle: On spreading chaff cloud for countering the terminal guidance missile
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a software platform which can simulate and study the countermeasure between the terminal guidance missile and the warship. A criterion for evaluating effectiveness of chaff jamming is studied and requirements of chaff RCS are discussed. Strategies of spreading chaff cloud and elusion of the warship are studied and verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Frequency-coded pulse radar imaging via compressive sensing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel compressive sensing (CS) based frequency-coded pulse radar (CS-FCPR) imaging approach is proposed in this paper. FCPR enables high resolution range and Doppler estimation, while transmitting narrowband pulses. Considering spatial sparsity of the radar target scene, FCPR targets echo is first analyzed and the problem of joint range-Doppler estimation is formulated to fit the CS classical framework. Direct solution of this problem using traditional sparse signal reconstruction algorithms needs the statistics of the noise. A cross validation (CV) based robust-SL0 (CV-RSL0) algorithm without requiring the prior information of the statistics of the noise is presented to extract the parameters of targets. The targets parameter extraction performance of the proposed algorithm can rapidly approach the lower bound of the best estimator with the signal to noise ratio improving. Numerical results are compared with the traditional matched filter to illuminate the validity and superiority of this method.

articleTitle: Application of Neural Network data associating method in the Radar Network system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For data association problem during the multiple targets tracking in the Radar Network system, we proposed a kind of improved Discrete Hopfield Neural Network (DHNN) data associating method. We used the parallel computation and optimization ability of DHNN, and improved the global optimization ability of DHNN by modifying the energy function of DHNN and applying the simulated annealing algorithm to the status's adjusting of DHNN. This method improved the tracking performance and shortened convergence time of the network. From the Monte Carlo simulation experiments, the association performance and compute velocity of the proposed method was proved higher.

articleTitle: Development of RF front-end with high T/R isolation for Ka band Mono-antenna FMCW radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The RF front-end with high T/R isolation for Ka band mono-antenna frequency modulation continuous wave (FMCW) radar is introduced in this paper. By using of balanced passive cancellation network, the transmitter's leaking signal is cancelled in receiving channel. Moreover, making use of orthogonal decomposition and cancellation principle for small reflecting signal in transmission line, the reflecting signal in antenna feeder due to mismatching is eliminated through introducing reflection cancellation tuner. Finally, more than 50 dB T/R isolation in 500MHz bandwidth is attained for radar front-end with greater than 200 mW transmitting power and less than 12dB receiving noise figure. The weight is no more than 150g.

articleTitle: Man-made structure height estimation via a single VHR SAR intensity image
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Height estimation of man-made structures in urban and suburban areas is an interesting but challenging problem, especially from single SAR image, which usually occurs in emergency response after crisis. A novel model based height estimation approach is proposed, which finds a best match between parameterized object model and the observed single intensity SAR image data. Firstly, a projection function for single bounce signal return between 3D object model and corresponding characteristic regions in SAR image is constructed, which make the model generation phase very simple and fast. Then, a new likelihood measure for the matching between the height hypothesis and the SAR data is proposed in the respect of image segmentation. The matching procedure is iterated until a global maximum similarity is achieved and then the height estimation is obtained, which is realized by the simulated annealing algorithm. The experiments performed on general terms of buildings in the simulated SAR image data set verify its validity.

articleTitle: An iterative carrier frequency estimate algorithm based on high-order cyclic cumulants
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The carrier frequency estimate algorithm based on high-order cyclic cumulants does not need a training sequence. Due to the fact that the high-order cycle can suppress the stationary and non-stationary Gaussian noise, the algorithm is tolerant to the noise mentioned above. The computation of the algorithm is deduced in this paper. It shows that if large searching range of carrier frequency and high frequency resolution are required, the computation will be great. In order to reduce the computation, an iterative carrier frequency estimation algorithm based on high-order cyclic cumulants is introduced in this paper. The simulations show that the algorithm proposed in this paper can reduce the computation significantly.

articleTitle: GMTI performance analysis of STAP based SBR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Space Time Adaptive Processing (STAP) can effectively mitigate the clutter in Space Based Radar (SBR) Ground Moving Target Indication (GMTI). This paper analyses Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and Signal-to-Interference-pulse-Noise Ratio (SINR) improvement in GMTI signal processing chain of a SBR system, describes the relationship between radar's GMTI capability with its design parameters, working parameters and processor performance. Simulation is also processed in this paper.

articleTitle: SAR imaging of dominant scatterers using cascading StOMP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We propose an algorithm for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging of dominant scatterers based on the theory of Compressive Sensing (CS). The SAR raw data is randomly sampled in two-dimensional, and the pulse compressing and azimuth focusing are implemented by stagewise orthogonal matching pursuit (StOMP). In order to preserve all energy of lower scatterers, two stage thresholds are designed while implementing pulse compressing. The experiments on real SAR data show that wide-scene image can be constructed using less data, without the loss of resolution.

articleTitle: Application of Relay Satellite Scheduling based on STK/X
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Tracking and Data Relay Satellite (TDRS) has been seen as bridge not only between user spacecrafts in LEO (Low Earth Orbit) or MEO (Middle Earth Orbit), but also between user spacecraft and groundstation. The paper firstly introduces the main function of STK and its components. Then based on the characteristics of Relay Satellite Scheduling, a scheduling system is designed with vc++/STK/X and validated by a set of typical operation datas. The result shows that the model can resolve small-scale relay satellite scheduling problems and reduce exploitative difficulty of application.

articleTitle: Ground emitters localization aboard deformable airframes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A processing for passive localization of ground transmitters from an aircraft is presented. It is fast and precise but has the disadvantage of being sensitive to structural deformations. A method of estimation and real-time correction of deformations effects is exposed.

articleTitle: Internal and external calibration of POLINSAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Polarimetric SAR interferometry (POLINSAR) techniques have been studied as hot research topics in the area of SAR remote sensing in recent years. At present, many POLINSAR systems were developed, and the first POLINSAR prototype in China is also developed by 38th Research Institute of CETC. There is an urgent need for the data from these sensors to be calibrated, so that the relationships between radar backscatter and geophysical parameters can be properly established. In this paper, we introduce internal and external calibration of POLINSAR. Then, the validation of calibration accuracy is implemented based on reflectors in experimental site. The results indicate crosstalk and imbalance can be improved after calibration.

articleTitle: Unsupervised change detection for remote sensing images using multiscale decomposition and treelet fusion: A level set approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: With the development of remote sensing technology, using remote sensing images to do change detection is gaining more and more attention. In this paper, a novel approach for unsupervised change detection is proposed. Firstly, SWT is used for multi-scale decomposition; then use treelet to fusion the reconstructed difference images at every level; finally, the change detection map is obtained through a level set segmentation. The effectiveness of our method is validated by experiments on five different data sets from different resources. By comparing with other state-of-art technologies, the results show that the proposed method yields better performance in most cases.

articleTitle: Adaptive waveform design for detecting distributed target in heavy sea clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Heavy sea clutter seriously depresses the detection of distributed target. In this paper, an adaptive PM waveform design method with evaluation factor is proposed to suppress clutter energy and improve the detection performance. Simulations illustrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Range-spread target detector based on AD test for non-Gaussian Clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper addresses range-spread target detection in spherically invariant random vector clutter (SIRV). A strong scatterers integrator based on Anderson-Darling test (ADT-SSI) is addressed for the problem that MSDD has detection loss when falsely estimating the number of scatterers. For ATD-SSI, adaptively estimating the number of target scatterers according to the observations, which can improve performance and robustness of the detector effectively.

articleTitle: Applying the log-cumulants of texture parameter to fully polarimetric SAR classification using Support Vector Machines Classifier
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a fully polarimetric SAR classification method based on the log-cumulants of texture parameter of the fully polarimetric SAR data. Unlike other classification algorithms that classify pixels by their scattering characteristics, this method will use a combination of the texture parameter of fully polarimetric SAR data and the Support Vector Machines (SVM) Classifier based on the spherically invariant random vectors (SIRV) model. A full polarimetric image Oberpfaffenhofen region in Germany, acquired by E-SAR at L-band, is used for our experiment. It is shown that the proposed method is consistent with the actual scattering mechanisms, especially for urban areas, and can be used to effectively distinguish different types of terrains.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation of multiple sources based on multiset canonical correlation analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: It is an urgent task to improve the direction of arrival (DOA) estimation precision. To solve the problem of time difference DOA estimation is sensitive to interference and noise, this paper proposes a novel multiple sources DOA estimation algorithm based on multiset canonical correlation analysis (MCCA). The key technique of this DOA estimation method is blind separated the mixed signals from multiple moving sources by MCCA, translated the multiple sources DOA estimation problem to each source DOA estimation in turn, and removed the effect of interference and noise. The simulation results suggest that the estimation of time difference after MCCA processing is more accuracy and stabilization than direct correlation and after CCA processing, can greatly improve the performance of DOA estimation.

articleTitle: MIMO radar signal separation algorithm in non-Gaussian clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of MIMO radar signal separation with traditional matched filtering (MF) in dependent non-Gaussian clutter, and a fractional lower order generalized sidelobe canceller (FLO-GSC) is proposed. In the proposed method, the dependent clutter and the undesired transmitting signals are regarded as interference. By using the fractional lower order statistics of the received signals based on the rule of minimum mean square error (MMSE), the FLO-GSC model is derived. Finally, simulations are given for the MIMO radar signal separation in SG-Alpha stable distribution clutter. The results show that the proposed method is efficient for MIMO radar signal separation in dependent non-Gaussian clutter.

articleTitle: ESPRIT matching pursuit algorithm for DOA estimation with single snapshot
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For a uniform linear array, classical DOA estimation methods, such as ESPRIT etc., with a space smoothing preprocessing, can be applied to the case of single snapshot. Due to the spatial sparsity, this DOA estimation problem can be translated into a sparse signal recovery problem. Then we can use some sparse recovery methods to resolve DOAs. As a highly efficient method among those, the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm is considered at first. It has been observed that OMP can offer DOA estimates with smaller mean-square errors than ESPRIT at low SNRs; however, an opposite conclusion will be drawn at high SNRs. Combining the advantages of the both methods, we present a novel ESPRIT matching pursuit (EMP) algorithm, which takes a full utilization of ESPRIT and a maximum correlation method in a process of greedy pursuit. Simulation results indicate that the presented method outperforms both OMP and ESPRIT at different SNRs.

articleTitle: 5Multi-objective waveform design for cognitive radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An important characteristic of a cognitive radar is the capability to adjust its transmitted waveform to adapt to the radar environment. The adaptation of the transmit waveform requires an effective framework to synthesize waveforms that could provide different trade-offs between a variety of performance objectives. In this paper, phase-coded waveform, whose modulus is constant, is considered to be synthesized to realize a smooth trade-off between maximizing output signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for a particular target and the mutual information (MI) between the received signal and the target response. A new iterative algorithm is proposed to synthesize constant modulus waveform to maximize SNR and MI simultaneously. Simulation results show that the performance of the synthesized waveforms is satisfactory and can approximate the ideal waveform.

articleTitle: Designing sparse frequency waveform with low range sidelobes for HFSWR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Sparse frequency waveform with narrow stopbands sparsely distributed over a wide spectrum band is desired for high frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR). However, it gives rise to high range sidelobes. To solve this problem, a method for designing sparse frequency waveform with low range sidelobes is proposed in this paper. The fitness function is constructed to design phase codes according to the following criteria: minimizing the ratio of the energy in stopbands to that in passbands with finite power constraint and minimization of range sidelobes. The particle swarm optimization-simulated annealing (PSO-SA) algorithm, by combing PSO with SA, is introduced to search the optimal unimodular solution. Simulation results are presented to show the effectiveness and flexibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A new method for the synthesis of sparse linear array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper discusses the problem of designing a sparse array with modified particle swarm optimization algorithm. As we can see from the simulation, the MPSO performs better and makes the array get a lower peak sidelobe level (PSLL).

articleTitle: Compressed sensing based ultra-wideband radar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A new CS-UWB radar model combined with the Meridian prior is proposed in a Bayesian framework in this paper. Simulations are carried out in the UWB radar system, which testify that the proposed model can not only reduce the sampling rate significantly, but also achieve a precise reconstruction.

articleTitle: FOPEN radar for UGS applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The very short range detection devices are the basic elements of Homeland protection and Homeland security systems. The Unattended Ground Sensors (UGS) are widely used to protect critical area and for border surveillance, in open area perimeters. FOliage PENetrating (FOPEN) radar are needed when the areas or the borders to control are located inside the forest or jungle, in both northern borders or equatorial locations. In this paper a Ground Moving Target (GMT) radar, working at UHF frequencies, battery operated, is presented together with the requirements and the performances obtained.

articleTitle: Potential of human detection with SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: ONERA performed specific acquisitions dedicated to human detection on SAR images. After briefly describing the experimental SAR platforms, this paper presents results of human detection obtained on high resolution SAR images at different frequency bands and results on change detection.

articleTitle: High resolution beamforming with promoted sparsity via reweighted methodology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We propose a high resolution beamforming method based on a strategy of reweighted compressed sensing. By solving the beamforming problem in a reweighted manner, a direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation result with enhanced resolution and precision can be obtained stably.

articleTitle: Multistatic target tracking in DAB/DVB-T networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper we present a tracking concept for multistatic passive radar systems based on DAB and DVB-T signals. We develop a strategy based on likelihood ratio testing that utilises a fixed threshold testing to distinguish between ghosts and targets.

articleTitle: Based on the covariance and coherency matrix for SAR sea oil spill observation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this study a method to enhance sea oil spill observation using covariance and coherency matrix with quad-polarized synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is proposed. The proposed formula is used to differentiate the backscattering from the oil spills and biogenic slicks.

articleTitle: A calibration method based on fusing multiple calibrators for UWB-VAR system using stepped frequency
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The system calibration is an important factor for the detecting effect of UWB-VAR (Ultra Wide Band Virtual Aperture Radar) which can penetrate the earth to explore the weak scattering target flush buried in the shallow seam. The regular system calibration method developed for high frequency narrow band radar is based on one single calibrator, which is not applicable to the UWB-VAR system owning to its ultra bandwidth and inconsistency of multi-channel. After the research on the system errors and the electromagnetism of both calibrators and landmines, a new method based on the fusion of multi-calibrators and multi-band is introduced in this paper. This new method would not only calibrate the system errors efficiently, but enhance the performance of imaging. Finally the real data has proved that such a method can be effective.

articleTitle: Angle estimation of coherent targets for bistatic MIMO radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Angel estimation is considered for bi-static MIMO radar in the case where there exist both coherent and incoherent targets. Firstly, the bis-tatic MIMO radar data model is introduced and data covariance matrix is given. secondly, a matrix is formed using a column of the bi-static MIMO radar data covariance matrix. The rank of the formed matrix is only related to the number of the targets. Finally, the estimation of signal parameter via rotational invariance techniques (ESPRIT) algorithm is applied on the formed data matrix to estimate the direction of departure (DOD) and the direction of arrival (DOA). The numerical results show the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Improved parameter weight method based on SWEDE for 2D DOA estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper proposes an improved PWM algorithm: SWEDE-PWM algorithm by combination of SWEDE and PWM algorithm. It can reduce the computation of 2-D searching and eigenvalue decomposition simultaneously. Application to noncircular signals to improve the performance is also considered.

articleTitle: A novel PN-coded FMCW radar design and implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a pseudo-noise( PN) coded FMCW radar system design and implementation is proposed, the PN-coded FMCW radar character as low false alarm rate and low cost, the radar sensor prototype has been used in a collision warning system. experiment results indicated that the radar is suitable for automotive collision avoidance system application.

articleTitle: An improved track-before-detection algorithm based on coherent integration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A new track-before-detect algorithm based on coherent integration is proposed. It applies coherent integration, mathematical morphology and directional weighting. Additionally, the successive L - 1 frames are used when deciding the transform state. The simulation results show that the improved algorithm performs well.

articleTitle: An optimization beam-position selection method based on genetic algorithm for Distributed Satellite-borne SAR system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: How to select optimal beam positions in Distributed Satellite-borne SAR (DSS) system is a big challenge. Even the world famous innovative spaceborne radar interferometer mission - TanDEM-X system implemented by the German Space Agency has also suffered an optimized mission plan period for reduction of data acquisition time and more balanced performance. In this paper, an optimization beam-position selection method based on genetic algorithm for DSS system is proposed. The beam-position selection process is described as a multi-objective optimization problem (MOP). Many details are analysed and designed, such as genetic encoding, structure of initial population, evaluation fitness function, design of genetic operators (selection, crossover, mutation). In the end, an optimization beam-position selection was made for TanDEM-X system. Through computer simulation, the method is proved to be effective.

articleTitle: Analysis of Radon-Fourier Transform in clutter background and optimal weight processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Radon-Fourier Transform (RFT) has been recently introduced as an effective method for long-time coherent integration of moving targets. In this paper, analysis of RFT in clutter background is proposed to prove its capability to separate targets from clutter. Furthermore, the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) Improvement Factor of RFT is introduced and calculated. Then, according to the SCR Improvement Factor, an Optimal Weight Processing is proposed in this paper, which can achieve the optimal SCR Improvement Factor. Finally, some numerical simulation is provided to demonstrate the results and conclusions.

articleTitle: A modified umbrella-shaped monopole antenna for multi-band operation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel multi-band monopole antenna that consists of Umbrella-shaped patch and slots cut out of the ground, fed by 50-Ω microstrip feed line is introduced. The antenna has simple structure with dimensions of 40 mm×40 mm. The simulated impedance bandwidth for -10 dB return loss is from 2.26 to 2.56 GHz, from 3.35 to 3.6 GHz, from 5.12 to 5.37 GHz and from 5.65 to 6.05 GHz, respectively, covering the 2.4/5 GHz WLAN and WiFi operating band and 3.5 GHz WiMAX operating band. Also, the omni-directional pattern, good gain, and broad bandwidth performance over the operating bands have been obtained.

articleTitle: Doppler laser radar for measuring target range and speed with high precision
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we describe an in-car laser radar schematic diagram, and propose a new modulation scheme for the in-car laser radar measuring target range and speed with high precision simultaneously. Then, we perform experiments to verify the correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Phase-only control of antenna shaped patterns with a genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Genetic algorithm (GA) is applied to shape the antenna patterns by modifying just the phase distribution in this paper. In order to form a given pattern for antenna arrays, the genetic algorithm is used to optimize the phase distribution of excitations. GA has been shown to be an effective strategy in the nonlinear optimization and it is fit for designing shaped-beam antenna array. This paper gives the example of a horn cavity whose opening is flared in H side with metal lens and the measured result that improve the validity and practicability of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-wave two-dimensional active phased array radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A millimeter-wave (MMW) two-dimensional (2D) active phased array radar is presented. This radar is composed of 16×16 low-cost T/R modules, four channels receiver with two wave bands, and a high-speed signal processor based on VPX bus. Some test and experiment results are described.

articleTitle: Subspace projection for adaptive generalized likelihood ratio detection in Compound-Gaussian clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Poorly parameter estimates seriously depress the performance of adaptive GLRT detector. In this paper, orthogonal subspace projection algorithm is adopted to suppress clutter energy and mitigate performance degradation due to parameters estimation error. Simulations illustrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: 3-D geometric feature extraction of vehicle target from 2-D high resolution SAR imagery based on shadow information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel method of 3-D geometric feature extraction of vehicle target based on the fusion of the shadow information from a very few (just 3 to 5) 2-D high resolution SAR imagery with different azimuth is proposed in this paper. And the validity of the proposed method has been proven by a large number of experimental results using MSTAR measured SAR imagery.

articleTitle: A signal-to-noise ratio enhancement method for non-cooperative bistatic radar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In non-cooperation bistatic radar system, the target detection performance of the system is degraded by the background clutter and random noise. In order to solve this problem, a new method based on signal phase matching for signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) enhancement is proposed. It fully uses the phase differences of target signals and interference signals. The target signals are successfully separated from the background clutter and random noise according to the signal phase matching. The simulation results show that this method can effectively suppress the background clutter and random noise and remarkably enhance the SNR of the non-cooperation bistatic radar system, which has important and practical significance in improving the target detection performance of the non-cooperation bistatic radar system.

articleTitle: Based on hybrid genetic algorithm for simulation research of antenna thinned efficiency
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In satisfies the array main lobe width, the hybrid genetic algorithm is used to optimize the antenna array and weight. Draw out the array elements from a 98×100 antenna array. After thinned, probably reduced 25% array elements, the side-lobe, gain, and main lobe width satisfies the predetermined request.

articleTitle: Monopulse Estimation of swerling I–II extended targets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Maximum likelihood estimators for the centroid and the extension of Swerling I-II extended targets are given which are based only on the outputs of the generalized monopulse ratio. The statistical performance of these quantities is characterized by mean and variance.

articleTitle: A noise resistant synchronization method and its application in chaotic radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A new synchronization control method for chaotic system, which only needs one scalar time series of the master system to reach the synchronization, is present in this paper. It is robust to noise and the synchronization can be obtained in a high level noise. This method is then used in noise radar system to get the target range resolution. Finally, numerical examples are given to illustrate when using the robust chaotic synchronization method, signal, the correlation performance has a clear peak, which makes it easy to get the target range resolution.

articleTitle: A wideband spatial filter bank architecture for synthetic range profile
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A wideband array imaging architecture based on subbanding and spatial filter bank is developed and its performance is analyzed in detail. By using the method called angle bin, the synthetic range profile can be acquired with accepted distortion. Two related theoretical formulas are deduced for the calculation of the range shift value and evaluation of the amplitude deformation extent of a target echo impinging upon the proposed subbands imaging architecture, and thereby two critical conditions are derived. When radar system parameters satisfy such two critical conditions, a target's filtered synthetic range profile with acceptable distortion can be obtained. Specific conclusions are verified with some simulation results.

articleTitle: A method of track association with systematic error
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The problem of track association with systematic error between radar networks is researched. ECEF (Earth-centered-Earth-fixed) coordinate is taken as the common reference coordinate, and multi threshold is used to carry out track association. The coarse threshold is based on the different sensors' measurement. The sampling variance that obtained by sequence error is taken as the history track correction threshold. Finally, the unsolved tracks are distinguished by global optimization method. The simulation result shows the effectiveness of the methods.

articleTitle: Scattering characteristics analysis of radar antennas in far field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The simulation of antennas' scattering characteristics is addressed, focusing on the antenna mode RCS. Three typical methods of antenna scattering analysis are presented, taking a microstrip antenna as an example. The results demonstrate the consistency and correctness of the above methods.

articleTitle: Design of a radiator array for one-dimension wide-angle scanning phased-array antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a 32×8 radiator array based on quasi-Yagi antenna is designed to satisfy the requirements of one-dimension wide-angle scanning phased-array antenna. The radiators are simulated and optimized with the 3D FEM full-wave simulation software Ansoft HFSS, and then a 32×8 radiator array is fabricated and its VSWR and radiation characteristics are measured. In X band, the frequency bandwidth is more than 20%, when the measured VSWR is less than 1.3, and the measured H-plane 3dB beam width is larger than 90°. The radiator array has satisfied the requirements of H-plane one-dimension wide-angle scanning phased-array antenna.

articleTitle: Minimum variance multi-frequency distortionless restriction for digital wideband beamformer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper proposes a digital amplitude-phase weighting array based a minimum variance multi-frequency distortionless restriction (MVMFDR) to aviod the frequency band signal distortion in digital beamformer and too short time delay line (TDL) requirement in analoge wideband TDL array.

articleTitle: X-band core T/R module with LTCC technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: LTCC technology (Low temperature co-fired ceramic) provides an effective way to decrease the volume of the system and increase the reliability of the system. A kind of vertical transition, depicted in this paper, is used widely in the T/R module. The structure and operation principle of T/R module are discussed. The design results in a small size (40.9×15×5.7mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) and low weight (10.1g). The measures module's output power is more than 40dBm, These results suggest the feasibility of building such a core T/R module for Space synthesis aperture radar application.

articleTitle: A method of tie points detection in InSAR block based on SVD
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A method based on Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) is presented to solve Tie Points detection in the interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) block. The core concept of this method is to construct a corresponding matrix through the eigen-decomposition of the dissimilar distribution matrix which characterizes the dissimilarity distribution of the two descriptors attached to each feature point. The combination of the corresponding matrix with the ratio of the second greatest to the greatest element attributes to TPs detection. The proposed method is validated by experiments on the four adjacent SAR image-pairs of different terrain.

articleTitle: A direct-path interference suppressing algorithm for shared-spectrum multistatic radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Via the reiterative Maximum Signal Minus Interference Level (MSMIL) criterion and adaptive beamforming, a novel algorithm is proposed to suppress both the mutual interference and strong direct-path interference for shared-spectrum multistatic radar. Numerical results show advantages of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Targets detection in SAR imagery with an optical scene mask through a change detector
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The paper presents a method to detect Targets in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images at a specified scene. Using the corresponding optical image of the specified scene, the potential regions of interests for Targets can be extracted off-line as a scene mask. Then, the SAR image can be co-registered with this scene mask and a change detector is used to detect the Targets only in the potential regions of the SAR image. Finally, the Targets can be located and detected with the change detection results. The experimental result shows that the proposed method can detect and locate airplanes well at the airport with a high resolution SAR image, and it obtains a high positive detection ratio and evidently decreases the probability of the false alarm. As a result, the proposed method fusing the SAR and optical data is appropriate in detecting airplanes at the airports, vehicles on the roads, ships in the harbours, and so on.

articleTitle: Radar image simulation of complex targets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel radar imaging simulator with precise simulation of geometry and relative simulation of radiometry, to assist target recognition. The simulator is based on an new visualization procedure and a Lambertian-specular mixture model. Simulated results are compared with MiniSAR image of airplane C-130 evaluating the efficiency.

articleTitle: A novel Alternate Polarization Array and its filtering performance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Considering the limiting factors of the Polarization Sensitive Array (PSA) in realization, a novel Alternate Polarization Array (APA) has been proposed for the first time. The filtering performance has been presented theoretically and numerically. APA has anti-jamming ability in both space and polarization domains, but quantity of equipment are cut by half compared with PSA. APA possesses of perspective in radar and other fields.

articleTitle: An imaging method for MIMO radar based on compressed sensing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Imaging algorithm based on compressed sensing (CS) is studied for multiple inputs and multiple outputs (MIMO) SAR using orthogonal code waveforms. It can reduce the sampling rate and improve reconstruction results compared with traditional SAR algorithms. Through modelling all the echoes of orthogonal signals, it can also reduce the range ambiguity caused be nonideal orthogonality of multiple transmitted signals.

articleTitle: The knowledge-based tracking using geographic information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To improve the tracking performance in non-homogeneous clutter environment, this paper presents a novel method via knowledge-based technique and multiple track management strategies. Simulation results show the advantages of the proposed method based on real DTED.

articleTitle: Doppler spectra from bound waves in wind-wave tank
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: There exist bound gravity-capillary waves that move at the speed of dominate waves on the ocean surface, besides free gravity-capillary waves that satisfy the dispersion relation. In this paper, we propose a theoretic model to predict the Doppler shifts and bandwidths of bound and free waves. Additionally, we carry out the wind-wave tank experiments on microwave backscatter from ocean surface. Comparing with the measurements for different polarizations, and wind speeds, the formulae can be used to predict the Doppler bandwidths of bound waves and free waves.

articleTitle: Analysis of amplitude modulation effect on pulsed passive coherent location system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to analysis the amplitude modulation effect caused by the rotating transmit antenna pattern, which results in pulses loss within the direct-path pulse train. The loss mechanisms of signal to noise ratio (SNR) were discussed for these modulation phenomena. The analytical expression of the peak output of cross-ambiguity function was derived, which correspond to the cases of pulses loss occurrence. Simulation results show that the maximum SNR loss is less than 4 dB in the worst case, and the SNR loss curves for various Doppler frequencies and different number of pulse loss are conformed to the theoretical analysis. The worst Doppler frequency estimation bias is about 0.75 times the frequency resolution cell when there is no ambiguity in Doppler estimation.

articleTitle: Research on moving target detection algorithm based on maximum mutual information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An algorithm is presented to detect moving targets in Passive Millimeter Wave (PMMW) images with dynamic scenes. This algorithm incorporates the maximum mutual information registration method for background registration, and frame difference method for detection. Experiments' results demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Landmine bistatic scattering function estimation from virtual aperture radar image
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Virtual aperture formed by multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array can obtain the high-resolution image, which contains bistatic scattering information instead of monostatic scattering information and thus can improve the discrimination performance of virtual aperture radar. In this paper, a bistatic scattering function estimation method is proposed to extract the landmine bistatic scattering information from the forward-looking virtual aperture ground penetrating radar image. The imaging model of virtual aperture is developed firstly. Based on the imaging model, the bistatic scattering function of a suspected object is estimated on the virtual aperture image of the suspected object using the space-wavenumber processing. The experimental results show that the proposed method can offer the bistatic scattering information to discriminate landmines from clutter.

articleTitle: An HRRP preprocessing method and its application in radar target recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: HRRP preprocessing takes a key role in radar target recognition based on HRRP. In this paper, an HRRP preprocessing method, including a modified range alignment method and denoising processing, is proposed to improve the recognition performance for the radar target with moving parts. This scheme has been used to process the real data of the radar target with moving parts. The experimental results show that using the modified algorithm can not only reduce the size of the templates and the computation complexity, but also improve the recognition performance.

articleTitle: Correlation evaluation of experimental and numerical modes of the clamp structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper the modal correlation of a clamp structure in a radar system is analyzed. Both experimental and numerical (FE) approach was applied. The aim of the research was to calibrate the dynamics model and conduct the design. Firstly, the LMS Test.lab modal analysis is systematically introduced, and the natural frequency and vibration modes of the structure are given. Furthermore, the simulated modal of the structure by FEM is calculated. Based on the results obtained in prior analysis, the comparison of modal results is discussed, and the pretreatment techniques of correlation are described. Finally, the results of modal correlation are got. The results show that the simulated model is effective. Those works will be the basis for further dynamic analysis.

articleTitle: UWB frequency agility monopulse tracking radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Technical means to improve radar tracking accuracy by way of wideband frequency agility is analyzed, and practical implementation and test results of an 8~18GHz ultra-wideband (UWB) frequency agility monopulse tracking radar are provided.

articleTitle: Algorithm design of Mode S downlink signal processing based on 20MHZ sampling rate
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Preamble detection, bit and confidence declaration are the most important part in signal processing of Mode S radar. If preamble detection or bit and confidence declaration algorithm do not perform well, it will affect error detection and correction. An effective algorithm to preamble detection, bit and confidence declaration based on 20MHZ sampling rate is proposed in this paper. Simulation results show that this algorithm is excellent in preamble detection, bit and confidence declaration.

articleTitle: Joint radar wideband beamforming and long-time coherent integration via Radon-Fourier transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For moving target detection via wideband digital array radar (DAR), this paper proposes a novel coherent integration method with Chirp-Z transform, i.e., space-time Radon-Fourier transform (STRFT), in element-pulse-range frequency domain to jointly realize the wideband digital beamforming (DBF) and long-time coherent integration. The proposed method may dramatically reduce the computational burden of the space-time coherent integration for modern wideband DAR with a large number of elements and a long integration time. Finally, some numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of noncoherent processing radar in compound-Gaussian sea clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For noncoherent processing radar working in compound-Gaussian distributed sea clutter environment, the probability density function of detection factor and the analytical expressions of the false alarm probability are derived, and simulations show that the results match the Monte Carlo simulations quite well.

articleTitle: The simulation software of Bistatic Forward-looking SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we design and develop the simulation software of Bistatic Forward-looking SAR on Windows with VC++. The software has three modules: Echo Generation, Imaging Process and Property Evaluation. We do some simulation experiments under the actual condition to confirm the usefulness of the software.

articleTitle: HRRP synthesizing in presence of observation data loss: A new way
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A high-resolution range profile (HRRP) is the phasor sum of the time returns from different scatters on the target located within a resolution cell. In this paper, based on geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) model, we analysis the whole process using traditional inverse discrete Fourier transform method (IDFT) to synthesis HRRP firstly. After that basis pursuit (BP), to obtain HRRP based on GTD model, is presented, which takes advantage of the fact that target HRRP is sparse in radar range window, so we can also obtain the synthesised range profile (SRP) correctly in presence of observation data loss. Compared with IDFT method, the SRP using sparsity as a prior (namely, using BP method) has higher resolution, lower sidelobe level and more robust to incomplete measurement data HRRP. Meanwhile, to avoid computational complexity in BP, we also presents greedy algorithm named Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) for approximating the solution of BP. Both theoretical analysis and simulation experiments illustrate the advantage of proposed method.

articleTitle: Novel thin void-layer thickness determination method for lossy media using GPR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a novel method to estimate void thickness with modified calculation formula in lossy media. Electromagnetic (EM) wave transmission character was first analysed in lossy media, and the seismic thin-layer theory was introduced to interpret GPR response of void layer. Then a calculation formula was deduced to express the relationship between dominant frequency amplitude and thickness. Finally, the original formula was modified by calibrated coefficient, which was estimated through least-square curve fitting method. Simulation results show that the proposed method extends the traditional thin-layer thickness determination method to lossy media, and improves the estimated accuracy greatly by the modified formula.

articleTitle: Integrative design of a compact oil-filled radar transmitter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The topologies of klystron transmitter are discussed, in term of the requirements of design and the present technology development, the practical scheme of the high power klystron transmitter has been confirmed. The integrated design solution, system component and the key technology of the high voltage oil tank are specially emphasized in detail. The control and protection system of the transmitter is briefly introduced. Finally, the development direction of high power klystron transmitter has been prospected.

articleTitle: SAR image despeckling via spatially constrained multiscale products
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a wavelet-based multiscale products scheme for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image despeckling. A compactly supported quadratic spline function that approximates the first derivative of Gaussian is employed in the scheme to decompose log-transformed SAR images. The multiplied results of the decomposed coefficients of adjacent scales consist of multiscale products. The multiscale products can sharp the important structures while weakening noise. A spatially selective neighborhood technique by iteratively selecting neighborhood system in the multiscale products is introduced in searching the important structure information. The influence of the spatial information is imposed on the multiscale products, instead of on the wavelet coefficients, which improves the capability of identifying important features. Experiments show that the proposed scheme is better in SAR image despeckling and preserving edges and detail information than other wavelet-based multiscale products methods.

articleTitle: Individual RFI classification based on chaotic characteristics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper provides an efficient approach to classify individual radio-frequency interference in high-frequency radars. By employing empirical mode decomposition as signal pre-process method, stable chaotic characteristics of individual radio-frequency interference are extracted. Based on these stable characteristics and treelike assembly classifier, individual radio-frequency interference can be effectively classified. Detailed real data experiments are finally provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A novel autofocusing algorithm for ISAR imaging based on sparsity-driven optimization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel algorithm of phase adjustment joint with ISAR imaging based on sparsity-driven is proposed in this paper. In the scheme, both phase adjustment and imaging are established in an optimization problem to seek for phase errors and reconstruct ISAR image by exploiting the prior sparsity of target scattering field. The novelty of this method lies in its capability of de-noising and overcoming phase errors, resulting in well-focused image. Besides, the optimization problem is solved by using fast Fourier transform and matrix Hardmard multiplication, promoting the efficiently. The experimental results using both simulated data and measured data confirm the validation of the proposal.

articleTitle: Adaptive-update-rate tracking based on modified IMM-PDA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An adaptive-update-rate tracking algorithm based on modified IMM-PDA is proposed to avoid tracking loss of maneuvering target tracking in clutters. When there is no valid measurement the association gate is enlarged appropriately according to a modified innovation covariance, which is obtained from the actual predicted measurement and the one under highest maneuvering level hypothesis. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for maneuvering target tracking in clutters.
