articleTitle: A mixed target data association algorithm for wideband radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Expanded target data association algorithm for wideband radar is researched. A mixed data association algorithm is proposed which mix high resolution range profile (HRRP) feature aided data association with traditional joint probability data association (JPDA) algorithm. It indicates that the algorithm proposed can combine advantages of the two algorithms and can insure the validity of data association.

articleTitle: Online synchronization technique of bistatic SAR and flight trial
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Online synchronization is a key technique for bistatic SAR system. Synchronization and system performance are closely related. In this paper, online synchronization technique of bistatic SAR system has been studied and the implementation block diagram has been provided. Hardware design and implementation of bistatic online synchronization system was finished. After integrating the online synchronization system into bistatic SAR system the flight trial of bistatic SAR has been successfully conducted and first bistatic SAR image in China has been obtained by adopting online synchronization technique.

articleTitle: (2D)2k-NNDA: Two-directional two-dimensional k-nearest neighbour discriminant analysis for target recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An image feature extraction technique, two-directional two-dimensional k-nearest neighbour discriminant analysis ((2D)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>k-NNDA), is presented from the viewpoint of the k-nearest neighbour (k-NN) classification, which is an extension of 2DNNDA based the idea of the nearest neighbour (1-NN) classification. Similar to 2DNNDA, (2D)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>k-NNDA makes use of the matrix representation of images and does not assume the class densities belong to any particular parametric family. (2D)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>k-NNDA is applied to target recognition and the results demonstrate that (2D)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>k-NNDA achieves at least the same or even higher recognition accuracy than the existing 2D subspace methods.

articleTitle: Targets identification method based on electromagnetic scattering analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Target electromagnetic environment is becoming increasingly complex, which calls for the more advanced target identification technology. By the way of radar network, target information could be received in all directions. However, under the influence of some uncertain factors such as target background environment and electromagnetic waves space propagation attenuation, the information received by each radar contains a great deal of uncertainty. As one of the important uncertainty reasoning methods, D-S evidence theory could solve the uncertainty problem caused by unknown. It is a very important step of D-S evidence to construct basic probability assignment. The paper has analyzed the electromagnetic scattering characteristic of targets in discernment frame efficiently and accurately by multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). Based on the analysis result and information received by radar, the basic probability assignment has been constructed by template matching method, and then the evidences have been combined by D-S evidence theory, by which target identification result could be obtained. In this paper, the numerical example has demonstrated that it is accurate and efficient to identify the target by this way.

articleTitle: SAR imaging simulation of shallow sea Sand Ridges with finger-like features
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a simulation model of shallow sea bathymetry imaging by synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is developed. With the model, influences of SAR parameters on Sand Ridges with finger-like features are studied.

articleTitle: Covariance matrix estimation method in compound Gaussian sea clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: As the radar resolution has increased, the statistics of the clutter have no longer been observed to be Gaussian. The performance of traditional detectors was decreased badly in non-Gaussian environment. This paper proposed a covariance matrix estimate algorithm of detector in non-Gaussian sea clutter. The technique is based on the fix-point(FP) estimator that the iterative initalization matrix is a toeplitz matrix. In this paper, the proposed technique estimator performance is compared with two other covariance matrix estimators in real sea clutter data.The simulation results show that the proposed method can enhance the detector performance in real sea clutter.

articleTitle: Multi-physics simulation of high power supply used in the radar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The multi-physics fields in the working of power supply are calculated with finite element method. The analysis of simulation includes the coupling distributions of temperature, stress and electromagnetic fields. The results of simulation can be used to estimate the fatigue life and improve the design of high power supply used in the radar so as to enhance its performance of EMC, heat dissipation and structure intensity.

articleTitle: Feature extraction and frequency response recovery based on rational approximation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In order to obtain the target position invariant features and to recover target frequency response accurately, the orthogonal vector fitting (OVF) algorithm is introduced to solve the rational approximation of frequency response problems in target scattering system. By replacing the polynomial basis functions with orthogonal basis functions, the method overcomes the problem of pathological matrix equation. Besides, it also uses the iterative strategy to reduce the linearization error. According to the characteristics that the target conjugate poles of frequency response appears in pairs, the state space analysis method is used to achieve a fast solution to the denominator of the zero point and the concrete realization of the iteration process is given. Theoretical analysis and experimental results prove that, by introducing OVF to target frequency response approximation, the method can effectively solve the morbid normal equation and reduce the linearization error problems. Furthermore, it can also approximate target frequency response accurately and extract the target poles.

articleTitle: Sparsity-based MIMO radar imaging method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The matched filter, as a popular method, has been widely used to image a target in the radar society. Nevertheless, there exists an important difficulty that the resolution of the image produced by the filter can be changed with the variation of the target's distance. In this paper a distinct imaging algorithm through the exploitation of the sparsity of the received echoes is presented for the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar imaging application against the difficulty involved in the matched filter. Furthermore, the constrained conditions for the array size and element interval are also presented. Different from the imaging algorithm based on the matched filter, the iterative greedy algorithm is used to image a target in this paper. Due to the exploitation of the sparsity of the received echoes, the cross-range resolution of the proposed algorithm can be higher over the given spatial scope. Numerical simulations are provided for testing our imaging algorithm.

articleTitle: Noncoherent versus coherent MIMO radar for joint target position and velocity estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Recent research indicates that one can obtain improved MSE performance from employing a coherent processing approach in MIMO radar with properly placed antennas. This paper demonstrates that the magnitude of these gains decreases with an increase in the product of the number of transmit and receive antennas if the antennas for the noncoherent system are also suitably placed, using a placement which is generally different from the one for the coherent processing approach. In particular, the mean square error (MSE) of the noncoherent system approaches that of the coherent system when the product of the number of transmit and receive antennas is sufficiently large. A theorem is presented for the case of orthogonal signals in temporally and spatially white noise-plus-clutter, but numerical results for nonorthogonal signals and colored noise-plus-clutter follow a similar pattern.

articleTitle: Propagation modelling over variable terrain using the two-way PE method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The parabolic equation (PE) method which deduced from the wave equation is the most precise one for predicting the radio propagation in troposphere, whereas the traditional algorithms only forecast forward-propagating waves but neglect backward-propagating waves giving rise to more error in the presence of irregular terrain boundary environment. Thus, in this paper, the recursive two-way parabolic equation modelling and its in-depth procedure is presented which can compute the forward propagation and backward propagation field over any irregular terrain enhance the computation accuracy and remedy the insufficiencies. Compared to traditional WAPE and GTD, the correctness and applicability of the model are verified by simulation results in the normal atmosphere over single knife-edge and couple triangles.

articleTitle: Research on sub-pixel accuracy displacement estimation for Passive Millimeter Wave multi-frame Imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Passive Millimeter Wave (PMMW) multi-frame Imaging displacement estimation is a key procedure before Super-Resolution Reconstruction. In this paper, a novel method based on Phase-Only Correlation and IDFT for motion estimation is presented. Experimental data demonstrates that the proposed algorithm yields higher accuracy sub-pixel level motion estimation and proves the effectiveness and adaptiveness of this algorithm.

articleTitle: An approach to correction of ionospheric phase contamination in HF skywave radar systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In high frequency (HF) skywave over-the-horizon radar (OTHR), radar signals are subjected to phase contamination as they propagate through the ionosphere, leading to severe degradation capability of OTHR radar, so that it needs to be corrected. According to the high spatial correlativity of the ionosphere contamination and the adjacent range cells are subjected to the same contamination, a new approach is applied to the ionosphere decontamination of OTHR echoes based on maximum likelihood estimation auto-focus method in ISAR and clutter suppression. The decontamination procedure is divided into two steps: firstly eigenvector projection is used to preprocess signals, and secondly using maximum likelihood estimation method to estimate contamination. The simulation and real data processing results show that the method is of effectiveness and robust performance on different kinds of ionospheric phase contaminations.

articleTitle: Adaptive cancellation in transmitted signal of repeating type jammer based on fractional delay filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In the work process of repeating type jammer, the transmitted signal always enters into the jammer's receiver and make it work abnormally. An adaptive interference cancellation structure based on LMS algorithm is suggested to solve this problem. However considering the wideband interference signal, we improved the structure. The focus of this essay is to utilize variable fractional delay filter to make the reference signal and interference signal aligned, thus to improve the effect of wideband signal cancellation. In addition, the structure of the variable fractional delay filter is given. Finally, the effectiveness of the adaptive cancellation in wideband interference signal by using this structure is proved through simulation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Pulse Compression for stepped frequency continuous-wave radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a sidelobes suppression algorithm for stepped frequency continuous-wave (SFCW) radar via the reiterative minimum mean-square error criterion. The results of simulations and real data show that the high range sidelobes are successfully suppressed by the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on a novel method for identification friend or foe based on fuzzy c-means and dynamic Bayesian network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper focus on the problems coming from uncertainty and target's time variation in the identification friend or foe, and solves them by using an algorithm combining fuzzy c-means(FCM) and dynamic Bayesian network(DBN). The simulations prove the algorithm's validity.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional ISAR imaging based On DCFT
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Estimating cross-range motion parameter is one of the most important steps while using antenna array to get targets' 3-D ISAR images. A method which can estimate cross-range motion parameter based on DCFT is proposed in this paper. It can not only lower the amount of computation, but also insure the imaging precision. The validity of the method would be proved by simulation.

articleTitle: Airborne GMTI radar target tracking by an effect UKF filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Tracking ground targets with GMTI sensors has been considered a challenging problem. This paper introduces a reformative unscented kalman filter for airborne GMTI radar tracking problem. A novel airborne GMTI radar observation model is proposed by analizing the airborne radar observations. To reduce the nonlinear relation between the Doppler observation and target state, Doppler observation is defined by a predigested distribution function. Experimental results show that the proposed approach is effective for airborne GMTI radar tracking with a low computation burden.

articleTitle: Speed measurement of permanent magnet synchronous motor in radar servo system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The speed measurement of radar servo system is discussed. It is based on the photoelectric incoder of the servo system. The realization and error of M speed measurement, T speed measurement are analyzed. The error curves are given by the experiment. The experimental platform is designed and the various methods are realized on it respectively. The designed M/T speed measurement method is realized. The experimental results showed: the designed and realized M/T speed measurement method have a wider measuring range than the other two methods. Its other measurement performance, such as measuring precision, is also improved.

articleTitle: An implementation of MIMO InSAR without transmitting orthogonal signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The ability of MIMO InSAR to reconstruct the terrain height profile would outperform the ordinary multibaseline InSAR. One key of implementing MIMO InSAR is the echo separation on the receiving end. However, the available orthogonal signals would introduce severe cross-interference due to their inadequate orthogonality for imaging. A feasible implementation of MIMO InSAR is presented in this paper, in which the antennas of MIMO InSAR would emit signals alternately in different pulse repetition intervals. Thus, the mainlobe echoes of signals transmitted by different antennas would return in different pulse repetition intervals coordinately, which implies the cross-interference could be suppressed sufficiently even with non-orthogonal transmitting signals as long as a low-sidelobe antenna is employed. The performance of the proposed implementation is proved via numerical simulations.

articleTitle: New imaging approach for MPC-MAB HRWS synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: High resolution and wide swath (HRWS) are the most important two requirements for modern synthetic aperture radar, but it is hard to satisfy these requirements at the same time. The advance of Multiple phase centre Multiple azimuth beam technology (MPC-MAB) had effectively released such conflict, and make the HRWS SAR imaging became possible. The principle of MPC-MAB SAR was investigated in this paper, and a new imaging approach based on adaptive down-chirp technology was proposed, imaging simulations were executed for both point and distributed target. All results proved that the imaging approach not only capable but also effective, and compared to traditional approach, it is can be easily operated and combined with classical imaging algorithms.

Author Keywords: Multiple phase centre multiple azimuth beam technology

articleTitle: Research on track generation technology for secondary surveillance radar(SSR) interrogator in interference environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For secondary surveillance radar (SSR), a new t rack generation technology is proposed. Firstly, the main processing of track generation is designed. Secondly, a new strategy of track correlation which combines the general association to the discrete association under the condition of interference environment is proposed, Finally, the adaptive filtering is discussed for track smoothing and prediction. The simulation results show that this track generation technology can improve the effect of track processing.

articleTitle: A novel PGA technique for circular SAR based on echo regeneration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Circular SAR (CSAR) can obtain images of high resolution. However, the image quality is very sensible to sub-wavelength motion errors caused by platform position uncertainty. Due to the limit of accuracy of the inertial measurement units (IMU) systems, a robust autofocus technique has to be used to cope with the demands of CSAR image formation. Because of the serious coupling between range and azimuth, and also the spatial-variant property of the phase error in the spatial frequency domain, the robust Phase Gradient Autofocus (PGA) technique that widely used in conventional spotlight SAR with a straight path can not readily be applied to CSAR. In this paper, a novel PGA technique for CSAR based on echo regeneration is presented to reduce the accuracy requirement from the order of a wavelength to the order of a range cell. The proposed approach is validated via simulation.

articleTitle: Adaptive targets detection in polarimetric high resolution radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An adaptive targets detector used in polarimetric high resolution radars is presented based on generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) criterion. The detector can ensure CFAR property for range-distributed targets in compound-Gaussian clutter. The simulation shows that the proposed detector achieves in general a better detection performance than its counterparts.

articleTitle: The applications of micro- nanofabrication technologies in T/R modules
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Transmit receive modules as the key part of active phased array antennas are focused on how to reduce the volume, weight, and improve the performance in high frequency. Micro- nanofabrication technologies can play a strategic role in improving the performance, functionality, and reducing the mass of transmit receive modules for active phased array antennas. This paper reports recent results on the micro- nanofabrication technologies such as thin film microwave circuits and nano optical elements. The thin film microwave circuits which are applied in transmit receive modules that have 50 μm line width and high density ground vias have been fabricated. The nano optical elements which are applied in optical detector that have finest width of 100 nm and aspect ratio of 7 and 13 have also been fabricated.

articleTitle: Design of 300W SiC wide band gap power module
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, the feature of SiC WBG semiconductor is introduced. Compared with Si and GaAs semiconductor, SiC WBG power devices have excellent performance of output power, power density, operating frequency, operating bandwidth and so on. The SiC WBG semiconductor has been used to power module, which is used at 0.8~1.4 GHz of P-band. The output power is 300 W. Firstly, the total frame and main functions are constructed. Secondly, the key techniques in the circuit are simulated and optimized, which include wide-band divider/combine and power amplifier. Furthermore, simulation results and circuits layout are deeply analyzed. Finally, figures and test data of amplifiers are also presented. SiC WBG power devices can operate in CW or pulse mode, as single amplifier or basic amplifying unit of power amplifier module in radar.

articleTitle: Challenges of ultra wideband, multi-mode radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Recent advances in wideband digital waveform generation, analog to digital converters (ADC) and high speed parallel processing provide the technology to develop ultra wideband systems for simultaneous synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and ground moving target indication (GMTI) modes. These systems are designed at either VHF or UHF frequencies to minimize the foliage attenuation and clutter masking of either terrain features or objects. The evolving challenge is to develop a common waveform for both SAR and GMTI, with emphasis on real-time signal processing.

articleTitle: A new method for parallel processing of real-time range compression
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Based on subbanding processing and amplitude-phase compensation, a novel fast and parallel method to realize big-sample-size range-compression (RC) in real-time SAR/ISAR systems is introduced. It is assumed that pulse compression will be performed in the subband domain. An innovative algorithm is presented that simplifies the design complexity of all FIR filterbanks used in the subbanding processing including the analysis filterbanks (used to decompose return signals into narrowband components), the synthesis filterbanks (used when combining subband components after processing), and the pulse compression generating filterbanks (used to generate subband pulse compression filters from a wideband pulse compression filter), and reduces filter orders, while guaranteeing RC performance. Moreover, it compensates the amplitude-phase errors caused by signal-generating and echo-sampling modules.

articleTitle: Radar signal simulation by stochastic modification of its experimental records
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Signal simulation is a very important tool in radar system design. Due to the complexity of radar signal structure the traditional approach to simulation needs calculation of the signal samples using an appropriate simulation algorithm. The definition of the algorithms should be preceded by tedious statistical analysis of the available signal data but the result of the simulation is not always satisfactory. This paper presents new approach to signal simulation that is based on manipulation of complete experimental signal records. In the proposed method of simulation the time consuming calculations of signal samples are replaced by generation of new signal samples on the model of the recorded ones. It is achieved by appropriate modification of real signal data respecting invariance of important signal feature(s) and is implemented by stochastic processing of the signal records. The identification of characteristic signal feature(s) is sine qua non condition of successful signal simulation. The proposed approach increases the efficiency of traditional method of simulation implementation useful among others for signal data bases construction.

articleTitle: Optimal waveform design for MIMO radar detection with clutter and noise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we introduce KL-divergence into MIMO radar waveform design to jointly resist clutter and noise. We derived the optimal waveforms which could match the target echoes and resist the background interference. Moreover, the energy allocation way is also used as the solution for distributing more energy into target channel and lower energy into inference channel. Finally, this paper shows the detection performance of optimal waveforms compared with other waveforms. Finally, numerical simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimal waveforms.

articleTitle: Bayesian track-before-detect for multisensor fusion systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The paper applies Bayesian track-before-detect to multisensor fusion systems, which can improve the detection and tracking performance of the fusion systems. In addition, centralized fusion architecture and distributed fusion architecture with corresponding fusion algorithms are proposed.

articleTitle: Feature parameter extraction approach with the stealth S-Cubed radar signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Radar equipments of stealth platforms such as aircrafts have adopted the newest modern technology to design the signal waveforms. One of the important and effective methods is the hybrid stealth radar waveform called spread spectrum stretch (S-Cubed). In this paper, the model of S-Cubed which combines linear frequency modulation (LFM) and discrete phase code is presented. Then, a novel approach based on phase difference and clustering is proposed for the feature parameter extraction of the intercepted S-Cubed. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has higher parameter extraction accuracy when the SNR is above 10dB.

articleTitle: Surface targets recognition by using the maximum likelihood estimator in remote sensing radars
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A new approach to recognize radar targets in imaging radars is presented. In this investigation, we deal with the statistical properties of the scattering mechanism for several types of radar targets, e.g., rough surfaces and vegetation canopies. For these targets, the use of deterministic techniques such as the target decomposition cannot be used alone. Therefore a statistical approach is applied to evaluate target parameters. Results show that this approach is a powerful tool to analysis of natural targets.

articleTitle: Polar format algorithm wavefront curvature compensation under arbitrary radar flight path
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An improved space-variant post-filtering approach to compensate the wavefront curvature effect in polar format imagery is presented in this paper, which is based on exploiting the endomorphism property of the polar format transformation. The main contribution of this paper is the construction of filter, which provides an accurate and general solution to wavefront curvature compensation. Point target simulation has validated the new approach.

articleTitle: On co-operative localization strategies using ESM & radar on board airborne platforms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper deals with some co-operative mechanisms involving both Electronic Support Measurement systems (ESM) and Radars aboard single or networked airborne military platforms to provide covert, long range or accurate targets localizations for situation awareness or targeting.

articleTitle: Airborne polarimetric SAR experiments with different crosstalk calibration techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: More and more people begin to realize the polarimetric calibration is important and necessary to the geophysical research and applications. In this paper, two kinds of polarimetric crosstalk calibration methods, including the one using only points target and the other one with distributed target, are compared and analyzed in details firstly. And then, an airborne polarimetric SAR data are applied to calibration with the methods by Quegan and Ainsworth. Finally, the experimental results and conclusions are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Stripmap mode SAR raw data generator for ocean scene with large squint angle
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A procedure for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) raw data generation for time-variant ocean surface is proposed. The appropriate ocean reflectivity function that takes account of the electromagnetic-ocean wave interaction is transformed on to SAR raw signal based on the distributed surface (DS) model. An efficient and accurate simulation algorithm with time-domain integration along range dimension for squint SAR raw signal is adopted. Moreover, the ocean's dynamics is accounted by means of interpolation based on the dispersion relationship of the time-variant waves. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the validity and applicability of the proposed techniques.

articleTitle: Realization of DBS imaging algorithm based on FPGA and DSP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: According to DBS imaging algorithm, this paper proposed the design of DBS imaging system. The design adopted the framework of DSP+FPGA, focusing on algorithm mapping, FPGA and DSP cooperation, and real time processing of radar signal data stream. Finally, the design was verified to be effective with measured data.

articleTitle: A realization of TBD in IRST system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Comparing with the Radar data, the data acquired from the IR system only has two dimensions for lacking of the information of distance, which results to the poor tracking performance and low reliability of targets. Based on TBD (Tracking Before Detect), this paper processes the IR data of aeroplanes which has been image-pretreated. For the low track reliability in tracking process, a cumulative track quality is produced. The track furcation, track combination, track deletion, and deferred decision logic is used to improve the robustness and the validity of track association. At the end of the paper, the processing result in real IR data shows the algorithm validity.

articleTitle: Space-time adaptive processing based on Beam-Doppler shift for bistatic radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Range dependence of bistatic clutter brings degradation of clutter suppression performance in space-time adaptive processing (STAP). The paper established clutter modeling of airborne bistatic radar, derived the analytical expressions of spatial and Doppler frequencies. Based on the clutter modeling and analysis of registration-based compensation (RBC) method, Beam-Doppler shift (BDS) technique to mitigate clutter range dependence in STAP was proposed, which transforms clutter snapshot into beam-Doppler domain and perform clutter spectrum registration. Owing to the processing of snapshots, BDS technique is easily performed. Computer simulations indicate BDS is affected less by FFT points number than RBC method, and has better performance in the case of giving attention to computation load.

articleTitle: Detection performance of MIMO passive radar systems based on FM signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper analyses the use of commercial Frequency Modulation (FM) broadcasting signals to configure a Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) parasitic (passive) radar system. The postulated system utilises multiple transmittters of opportunity, operating at multiple frequencies, with spatially distributed receivers. By utilising the Neyman-Pearson hypothesis, this paper addresses detection issues for such a MIMO parasitic radar system. Closed-form expressions for calculating the probability of detection with a given probability of false alarm has been derived. Lastly, Monte Carlo simulation results confirming the theoretical derivations are presented.

articleTitle: Efficient radar data processing algorithm for dense cluttered environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The most challenge of early warning balloon-borne radar (EWBR) is how to tracking small slow-moving targets. Because of the low detect velocity threshold, there are large numbers of uncertain measurements, such as reports from the ground traffic vehicles and reports from the clouds. Therefore, the data processing is very difficult to process the dense clutter measurements. An efficient data processing algorithm for the early warning balloon-borne radar is presented. The proposed algorithm combines a clutter map technique with a track-oriented multiple hypothesis tracking (TOMHT) method. Clutter map is used to reduce clutter and supply prior environment knowledge to MHT which can improve target tracking performance by adaptive parameter control. The algorithm's real time performance is proved by real radar application. The results indicate that the algorithm can reduce considerable false track rate and improve tracking performance.

articleTitle: System design and experimental results of polarimetric SAR interferometry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Polarimetric SAR interferometry (POLINSAR) is a very promising technique by combining polarimetric technique and interferometric technique. It can be applied to the area of remote sensing and measurement of structure over forest terrain. At present, many POLINSAR systems were developed, and the first POLINSAR prototype in China is also developed by 38<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> Research Institute of CETC. Lots of data are acquired by these systems, so POLINSAR techniques have been studied as hot research topics in the area of SAR remote sensing in recent years. In this paper, we introduce design of the POLINSAR prototype and some experimental results. This system can obtain 2m elevation accuracy by data processing.

articleTitle: Optimal waveform for detecting rank-one targets in waveform-dependent interference
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The design of optimal waveform for enhanced detection of rank-one targets is addressed. Rather than simultaneous design of waveform and matched filter maximizing the clutter-plus-noise ratio (SCNR), we design the optimal waveform maximizing the probability of detection under the Neyman-Pearson (NP) criterion.

articleTitle: OPCDM-LFM waveforms design for Formation-Flying Satellite radar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Formation-Flying Satellite radar system can fundamentally improve radar imaging performance by using a group of specially designed orthogonal waveforms. Based on studying the performance of LFM signal and phase coded signal, we modulate the same LFM signal using different phase coded signals, and generate the orthogonal phase code division multiplex linear frequency modulation (OPCDM-LFM) compound waveforms. The genetic algorithm is introduced to numerically optimize the compound waveforms. The simulation results show that the synthetic performance of the proposed waveforms in range resolution, orthogonal performance, Doppler tolerance and the utilization ratio of bandwidth is very well.

articleTitle: A Time-Varying Space-Time Autoregressive filtering algorithm for space-time adaptive processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To remedy the performance degradation of the original space-time autoregressive (STAR) filtering algorithm when operating in nonstationary clutter environments, this paper proposes a new type of STAR algorithm that invokes the time-varying autoregressive (TVAR) model and is called time-varying space-time autoregressive (TV-STAR) filtering. We demonstrate that, in the nonstationary clutter environment, the TV-STAR algorithm exhibits a commensurate performance with respect to the stationary case while the STAR filter totally fails due to “model-mismatch”. Meanwhile, TV-STAR is shown to offer a favourable convergence rate over reduced-rank STAP techniques such as loaded sample matrix inversion (LSMI) method. Simulated data as well as two sets of measured airborne radar data are used to demonstrate the performance of TV-STAR algorithm.

articleTitle: Centralized multisensor general association algorithm based on data compress technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Aim to solve the problem that the memory of the centralized multi-sensor system is easy to be saturated, this paper has proposed a new algorithm named centralized multi-sensor general association algorithm based on data compress technique against a background, which has a relative demand of real-time and tracking precision. In this algorithm, the measurement sets associated with the same target from each sensor are obtained and compressed into equivalents. A lot of association hypotheses are built with the equivalents, the remainder measurements and the track of each target. The score of every hypothesis could be obtained with the formula of the score function in multi-sensor general association algorithm, and the state estimation of the fusion center is gained finally. The simulation results show that this algorithm could track the targets effectively with the high density clutter and the general performance of this algorithm is better than that of sequential centralized multi-sensor joint probabilistic data association algorithm and parallel centralized multi-sensor general association algorithm.

articleTitle: The application of edge technique in wind lidar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The principle of single-edge technique and double-edge technique in the application of wind lidar was analyzed in detail, and the sensitivity and error of velocity measurement were discussed contrastively. The principle of single-edge technique is to compare the transmission of high resolution filter in two different frequencies. Double-edge technique lies in deducing Doppler shift as well as wind velocity value by comparing the intensity difference between two filters' output signal. And Mie and Rayleigh backscattering signals can be measured separately via selecting special working point. The analysis indicates that the velocity measurement sensitivity of double-edge technique is twice as much as that of single-edge technique in the same measurement condition. Although signal beam splitting of double-edge technique impacts SNR (signal-to-noise ratio), the velocity measurement error is still higher than that of single-edge technique.

articleTitle: Automatic bridge detection in SAR images based on fuzzy support vector machine and distance space
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel bridge detection algorithm based on fuzzy support vector machine (FSVM) and distance space is proposed in this paper. The experimental results show that the used strategy is effective for bridge recognition.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive beamformer based on convex optimization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A new adaptive beamform method is proposed. In this method, two inequality constraints have been used, which restrict not only the minimum gain in the interesting look direction but also the maximum value of the squared norm of the weight vector. The interior-point method is used to acquire the optimal solution. Simulation results show that this new method not only can avoid the signal cancellation phenomenon when the signal of interesting is contained in the beamformer training cell data, but also can be fitted with the small steering vector errors and the small number of snapshots.

articleTitle: Detection of the air maneuvering target based on the reconstruction of time sampling in the airborne radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An algorithm for detection of the air maneuvering target based on the reconstruction of time sampling is proposed. Space sampling is used to reconstruct time sampling, which is equivalent to increasing the number of time sampling in one array element. So the problem that the estimation precision is low when using the fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) directly is solved, which is caused by the limited pulses transmitted by the airborne radar in a Coherent Processing Interval (CPI). This algorithm improves the estimate precision significantly. Simulation results are provided to testify its validity.

articleTitle: Design of sea clutter data acquisition and analysis system with FPGA and USB2.0
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In order to testify the algorithms for the detection of wake targets in strong sea clutter background, a system which is used to acquire and analyse sea clutter data is developed. The system uses USB2.0 as the interface with microcomputer and works with FPGA as its kernel chip. Experimental results show that it can satisfy the data acquisition tasks of many kinds of radar and has a wide range of application.

articleTitle: A new amplitude probability density function estimation method for IPIX Grimsby data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper performs a fundamental analysis and a new amplitude probability density function (PDF) estimation of experimental data collected by McMaster University IPIX radar at Grimsby. Results demonstrate advantages of the new method over convenient regular histogram PDF estimation.

articleTitle: Design approach for axially symmetric dual-reflector small cassegrain antenna considering mechanical implementation constraints
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An easy-to-do procedure to design axially symmetric small Cassegrain antenna from prescribed geometric parameters is presented. In practice, the design of such an antenna is often restricted by mechanical implementation constraints. In this paper, we justify those geometric parameters of the antenna that can be directly controlled to fulfill these mechanical constraints. The rest of the parameters are assigned reasonably to provide antenna's optimum performance in gain and etc. Indeed, the design leads to such a smaller antenna.

articleTitle: Adaptive detection and sidelobe signal rejection for MIMO radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Antenna beam pattern in MIMO radar systems, like any other radar, exhibits sidelobes. Naturally it is possible for clutter and other sort of interference to be detected accidently via these sidelobes. This has the effect of mis-aligning the main beam steering vector and reducing detection performance. In addition, the performance is dependent on the precision of the array calibration process. This paper examines the competing effects of both those components. Specifically, we examine adaptive processing that operates across the whole MIMO system aiming to reduce sidelobe clutter, restore the steering vector to its true position and hence maximize signal to clutter ratio and therefore detection performance. The MIMO version of an Adaptive Detector with Conic Acceptance and Rejection (ADCAR) is developed, resorting to a generalized likelihood ratio principle. Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) properties of the detector are demonstrated. The performance of the MIMO- ADCAR is numerically evaluated. The results show the proposed detector is capable of achieving a compromise between sensitivity of mainlobe signal and rejection of sidelobe signal.

articleTitle: Radar embedded communication technology study
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Because of significantly merit in anti-jamming, potential performance, multifunction and integration, the technique and application of dual-use of radar and communication has been paid a special attention recently. This paper describer importance and latest techniques of radar embedded communication, analyses commonness and difference of Joint radar and communication. Based on rapid development of relative techniques, an concept of radar embedded communication with combining of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) was presented. Radar performance and communication capacity was studied. The prospect and further work are putt forward.

articleTitle: Research on registration of PMMW and visible images using silhouette extraction and multi-peak search based on fourier-mellin transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Gray-scale difference between Passive Millimeter Wave Imaging (PMMW) and visible images has challenged traditional registration algorithm applied within this field. In our paper, a hybrid algorithm that features silhouette extraction and application of FMT registration method is proposed and proved effectively and precisely.

Index Terms: Root Mean Square Error Of Cross-validation

articleTitle: Block-wise bivariate shrinkage functions for speckle reduction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The reduction of speckle in SAR image is important for SAR images processing. In this paper, we present an efficient despeckle algorithm based on dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) and bivariate shrinkage functions. A block-wise despeckle method is proposed to exploit the dependence between the coefficient and its neighbours. Experiment results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm shows great advantage in speckle reduction over the original bivariate shrinkage algorithm.

articleTitle: Matched illumination waveforms design for range-spread target in heterogeneous clutter plus noise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of matched illumination waveforms design based on the prior knowledge of the target scattering center models. Firstly, the properties of the target scattering model are discussed. Then, based on these properties, matched waveforms design on the principles of minimizing minimum mean square error (MMSE) and maximizing signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio (SCNR) are investigated. Finally, simulation results are shown that the matched illumination waveform increase the output SCNR significantly.

articleTitle: A new phased array structure to realize limited-2D-scanning
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A new array structure, which is called ladder array, is presented in this paper. This structure obviously reduces the grating-lobe amplitude of limited-2D-scanning phased array; besides, another advantage is the convenience of design, fabrication and beam control, which means the realizability of engineering.

articleTitle: A quantitive method to assess monopulse radar seeker angle measurement performance in the presence of noise jamming
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This Paper gives detailed mathematical equations and simulation method to quantify the monopulse radar seeker's standard and Home On Jamming (HOJ) angle measurement performance under multiple jamming, comparison between the theoretical results and simulation results are given at last, it is proved that both the theoretical method and the simulation method are correct in assessing the angle performance of the radar seeker in the presence of noise jamming.

articleTitle: MAR-model-based adaptive detection in space-time colored compound Gaussian clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The problem of adaptive detection for a multichannel signal in space-time colored compound Gaussian clutter is studied. The speckle component of the clutter is modeled as a multichannel autoregressive (MAR) process. Firstly, assuming that the MAR parameters are known, we derive a parametric generalized likelihood ratio test (PGLRT) against compound Gaussian clutter. By replacing the ideal MAR parameters with their estimates based on training signals only, the adaptive PGLRT detectors are obtained. The simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive detectors in training-limited situations.

articleTitle: Multi-channel target cooperative detection in through-the-wall-radar imaging based on random sparse array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper mainly deals with target detection under heavy clutters in through-the-wall-radar imaging, and based on random sparse array, proposes an approach of multi-channel target cooperative detection with modified N-K detector applied to multiple single-channel images.

articleTitle: Knowledge-aided adaptive subspace detection in partially homogeneous environments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we consider the adaptive subspace detector for partially homogeneous environments. In this environment, the clutter covariance matrix (CCM) of secondary data is equal to the CCM of the cell under test (CUT), except for a real constant factor. We also suppose that we have some prior knowledge of the CCM, which is controlled by the parameters of the statistics distribution of the CCM. Based on the Bayesian framework, a knowledge-aided adaptive subspace detector (KA-ASD) is given, and can be used to detect the subspace signal in partially homogeneous environments. The computer simulation is used to validate that KA-ASD is outperform the conventional subspace detector, and especially within a small number of training samples and coherent pulses.

articleTitle: The Study of realization method for the sliding spotlight mode in SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In the paper, the different characteristics between the spotlight mode and the sliding spotlight mode of spaceborne SAR are discussed. The system index, especially, antenna azimuth steering angle etc of sliding spotlight mode are studied. The realization method of the mode is presented, At the same time, the Doppler de-ambiguity, the requirement of azimuth steering angle, and the dwell time of azimuth point targets, and the position of rotation center are analyzed. The simulating results provided these analysis are rationality, and could be applied to the high resolution SAR system design.

articleTitle: Adaptive super-resolution algorithm based on PCA and wavelet for passive millimeter wave imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive super-resolution algorithm which calculates the regularization operator and parameter based on PCA and wavelet (APW algorithm) is proposed. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enhances the PMMW image resolution and has lower mean square error.

articleTitle: A CFAR algorithm for the non-homogeneous clutter background
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents an improved algorithm, Zoning 2-D CFAR, for the detections in a non-homogeneous clutter background. Numerical results show that the false alarm rate is successfully controlled in the severe clutter environments.

articleTitle: Order-statistic-based subspace detector for range and Doppler distributed target
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A detector based on order statistics is derived for adaptive detection of the distributed target in spherically invariant random vector clutter. The distributed target, which is modelled as a subspace random signal, may be distributed both in range and also in Doppler frequency axes. Firstly, the deterministic scatterer model generalized likelihood ratio test based on order statistics (OS-DSM-GLRT) is devised. Then an adaptive detector is obtained by replacing the number of range cells h<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and the normalized clutter covariance matrix with their estimation, respectively. The performance assessment conducted by Monte Carlo simulation confirms the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed detector.

articleTitle: A microstrip reflectarray antenna with the properties of wide bandwidth and low side-lobe level
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A portable radar substitutes the microstrip reflectarray antenna for the traditional paraboloid antenna to realize the intent of its portability and miniaturization. The difficulty of the design of the antenna is how to keep the low side-lobe property in the whole working band of the radar. A phase shifter scheme of the microstrip delay-line was used to realize the property of low side-lobe of the microstrip reflectarray antenna. The match fundamental that the microstrip patch and delay-line were satisfied with the relationship of linear phase shifter was adopted to realize the property of wide bandwidth and low side-lobe level of the antenna. It was proved in the testing result that the side-lobe level of the microstrip reflectarray was below −25dB in the 3.2% bandwidth of the X-band in the base of the more 50% efficiency of the antenna.

articleTitle: Polarization selectivity and optimization of thinned array for millimeter wave radar seeker with conformal phased array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel criterion for thinned array optimization based on optimal polarization (minimization of the cross-polarization level) is proposed to suppress the cross-polarization level and solve the problem of grating lobes arisen from thinned array in Millimeter wave conical phased array. The mathematical model based on the radiation pattern of the radar seeker polarization is developed firstly. Then the optimal polarization mode is chosen by comparing the cross-polarization level of circular polarization with that of linear polarization, and then two groups of basic parameters are determined. Finally, the modified particle swarm optimization algorithm is applied to optimize the configurations of the elements, while suppressing the grating lobes effectively. Simulation results verify the rationality of the proposed principle.

articleTitle: Investigation on compact polarimetry in SAR interferometry using CETC38 airborne data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper we investigate the classification performance of the compact polarimetric interferometric SAR (C-PolInSAR). The stressed compact modes are π/4 mode and CTLR mode, due to DCP mode equivalent to CTLR mode in theory. First, we provide a state-of-art of the C-PolInSAR modes, and present the different reconstruction algorithms aiming at recovering the full PolInSAR information from the observed C-PolInSAR dataset. Then, an assessment on the classification performance of the C-PolInSAR modes are carried out based on the Wishart ML classifier. Our emphasis is comparisons between the classification results of the C-PolInSAR modes and the corresponding reconstruction modes, versus the dual PolInSAR (D-PolInSAR) and the full PolInSAR (F-PolInSAR) systems. We test on the first PolInSAR dataset in China: CETC38 airborne data. Experimental results show that the C-PolInSAR has a promising application in the terrain classification, and it is an efficient alternative to the F-PolInSAR and the D-PolInSAR.

articleTitle: Compressive direction finding with robust sparsity prior
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a novel compressive sensing (CS) model is proposed for the robust direction finding problem. A new distribution prior with enhanced sparsity constraint is considered in the proposed CS framework. The simulation results as well as the real data processing exhibit its great superiority than many other spectrum estimation methods especially under the highly-corrupted condition1

articleTitle: Target position for squint-looking SAR based on doppler parameter estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For the squint-looking synthetic aperture radar (SAR), this paper quantitative analyzes the effect of Doppler parameter estimation errors on the static target position. The position of target can be analytically given in the ultimate SAR image with the estimated Doppler parameters with errors. Different from the side-looking SAR, it is found that not only the estimation error of Doppler centroid but also that of Doppler rate estimation will affects the target's position on the image. Finally, the numerical experiment results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of measured UWB RCS on high-resolution imaging in bistatic SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To obtain high-resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images, large signal bandwidth and wide accumulated angle are required. Based on space-surface bistatic SAR (SS-BSAR) geometric configuration, the amplitude and phase characteristics of measured Radar Cross Section (RCS) in ultra-wideband (UWB) radar are analyzed in this paper. According to the principle of monostatic and bistatic equivalence, the impact of the amplitude and phase characteristics of measured RCS in UWB radar on high resolution imaging in Bi-SAR is studied. By the simulation with the measured UWB RCS, it is found that high-resolution Bi-SAR images of target have significant difference in different bistatic angles and different target postures; even an obviously false target appears. The work of this paper will lay the groundwork for high-resolution imaging mechanism and image interpretation of Bi-SAR.

articleTitle: Extracting weak signal from passive coherent location radar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: By applying specified time-delayed correlation matrices, an algorithm for extracting desired echo in passive coherent location (PCL) system is proposed. Some experiment results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-targets detection in DBS via keystone transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Doppler Beam Sharpening (DBS) is a technique which can improve the resolution of radar azimuth. Aimed at the problem of range walk through resolution cell in DBS imaging, a new algorithm which corrects the range walk based on keystone transform is proposed. In this algorithm, a linear transform on the received data is employed to correct different range walk values without requiring the kinetic information and the look angle of the radar platform in the multi-targets environment. This method can realize coherent integration in azimuth dimension and improve the azimuth resolution. A fast implementation of keystone transform is used to satisfy the real-time processing of DBS imaging. Numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Doppler Centroid estimation for Space-Surface BiSAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Doppler Centroid estimation is a crucial problem in Synthetic Aperture Radar(SAR). In Bistatic SAR (BiSAR) phase synchronization error and Doppler phase have nearly the same form; Doppler centroid can not be estimated in traditional way. A Doppler centroid estimation method is proposed for Space-Surface BiSAR system through phase-cancellation of Dual-channel direct signal. Through phase cancellation, phase synchronization error can be counteracted while Doppler phase is reserved and Doppler centroid can be estimated from the reserved phase. This method needs little prior information and can suppress phase noise.

articleTitle: Improved wiener filter super-resolution algorithm for passive millimeter wave imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The problem of poor resolution of acquired image in the passive millimeter wave imaging stems mainly from antenna size limitations??thus necessitating some efficient post-processing to achieve resolution improvements. In this paper, we propose an improved wiener filter super-resolution algorithm. The algorithm uses iterative process of incremental wiener filter in wavelet threshold shrinkage to remove noise and increase the restored image information. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm enhances the resolution and reduces the ringing effects which are caused by regularizing the image restoration problem. Furthermore, the algorithm is easily implemented for passive millimeter wave imaging.

articleTitle: Noise radar interception using the principle of signal matched-phase
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A noise radar transmits non-sinusoidal signals which are ultra-wideband and continuous. Theory and experiments show that the noise radar has excellent properties of low probability of interception (LPI). In electronic countermeasure (ECM), the LPI feature of the noise radar brings great challenges to the radar interception. This paper presents a method for noise radar signal detection, based on the principle of signal matched-phase. At the same time, an improved signal matched-phase algorithm is presented, using a posteriori Wiener filter. The improved algorithm reduces the impact of background noise fluctuation. The simulation result shows that the method can considerably improve the signal-to-disturbance power ratio (SDR) and increase the probability of intercepting the noise radar signals.

articleTitle: DPCA motion compensation technique based on multiple phase centers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: DPCA technique is a principle technique for ground moving target detection, but DPCA condition of platform velocity, PRF and phase centre distance should be satisfied. The errant of platform velocity can destroy the condition usually. DBF technique is a flexible beam forming technique, by which multiple phase centers for receive beam can be formed. This advantage is used in this paper to form multiple phase centre distance for satisfying DPCA condition by real platform velocity. Numerical experiments verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Design and implement of a spaceborne MIMO SAR simulation software
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Radar signal models and software architecture for spaceborne MIMO SAR simulation are designed in this paper. Spaceborne MIMO SAR signal simulation is separated into several monostatic and bistatic signal simulation tasks. A parallel task decomposition method based on cluster computer environment is proposed to solve the problem of the large requirement of computation and memory. Finally, a typical spaceborne MIMO SAR simulation is executed and experiment results are presented.

articleTitle: Crashed plane detection based on the fusion of CFAR detection and polarimetric decomposition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Aiming at the problem of high false alarm rate and missing rate with single detection method, an improved target detection algorithm for crashed plane detection is proposed in this paper. The method firstly detects the possible existence of the crashed plane with Yamaguchi decomposition and Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR). Then, the detection results of the two methods are processed by pre-determination, and the final result is achieved by fusion and complementary detection. Simulation experimental results with real polarimetric data from NASA/JPL UAVSAR system demonstrate that the proposed method decreases the false alarm rate and missing rate effectively.

articleTitle: DOA estimation algorithm based on FFT in switch antenna array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An algorithm for fast DOA estimation in single-channel antenna array is proposed for the high complexity and low timeliness of the present algorithms. This algorithm applies the spatial FFT of multi-channel antenna array to single-channel antenna array. It takes the switching time into operation to construct the new transformation function, which can be utilized to operate spatial FFT to the sampled data of single-channel antenna array directly. Based on this, the SAA-FFT algorithm fitted for single-channel antenna array is proposed. The theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate that the algorithm is effective.

articleTitle: Space-surface bistatic SAR-GMTI
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A space-surface bistatic SAR-GMTI algorithm is proposed here and the clutter characters are also discussed. Then a reference signal is adopted for range compression, which can make the range cell migration and Doppler centroid decreased largely. Furthermore, the clutter Doppler and phase are analysed as well as the phase difference characteristics, a phase compensation function is constructed for clutter rejection as well. At last, simulation result verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Range-dependent clutter cancellation method in bistatic MIMO-STAP radars
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of cancelling range-dependent clutter in bistatic radar by using multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques. The rotation and projection operations are applied directly to the received data samples to transform the range-dependent clutter to be range-independent. Only the velocities of transmitter and receiver are needed to aid the data processing. The method exploits the fact that the clutter spectra of bistatic MIMO radar are in a 3-dimension (3-D) plane when both transmitter and receiver are side-looking. Simulation and analysis show that the proposed method is easy to implement and can cancel the range-dependent bistatic clutter effectively.

articleTitle: High resolution SAR performance limitation by the change of tropospheric refractivity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The imaging performance of high resolution airborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) system can be affected by phase errors resulted from the change in refractive index in the troposphere. Using the Hopfield model, we analyze the change in tropospheric refractivity, and give a calculation method for the apparent range between radar and a ground target. The mechanism in which the change in refractive index affects the high resolution airborne SAR performance is also analyzed. With a numerical calculation method, the maximum detection ranges of X-band and Ku-band SAR with different resolutions are obtained, and effects of the atmospheric refraction on the SAR image focusing are studied by simulations.

articleTitle: Design of an novel ultra-wideband antenna with dual band-notched characteristics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna fed by microstrip-line with dual band-notched characteristics is presented in this paper. The 3.5 / 5.5GHz dual band-notched characteristics are obtained by inserting a C-shaped slot to the radiating patch, and embedding a pair of inverted L-shaped slots into the ground plane respectively. The proposed antenna is simulated by the HFSS software, than; the prototype antenna is fabricated and measured. The measured results show that the good patterns and gains within the operating frequency band are obtained.

articleTitle: SAR signal modeling and imaging of a moving target
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Modeling of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) signal and image reconstruction of a moving target is considered. SAR topology and mathematical expressions of SAR signal formation called direct transform are analytically described based on three-dimensional (3-D) geometry, linear frequency modulated (LFM) waveform, and reflectivity function of the target. Image reconstruction equation named inverse transform including two Fourier transforms and phase correction is derived. Polynomial phase correction algorithm for SAR imaging of a moving target is developed. To verify the SAR geometry, signal modeling and image reconstruction scheme of a moving target a numerical experiment is carried out.

articleTitle: Detection ground slow moving target by airborne Along- and Across-Track interferometric SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Detection ground slow moving target by airborne Interferometric SAR (InSAR) with Along- and Across-Track baseline is a challenging issue. The terrain clutter and the terrain interferometric phase are the two main factors that are coupled into the real Along-Track Interferoemtric (ATI) phase caused by moving target's velocity. In this paper, based on the analysis of the comprehensive moving target's interferometric phase model, a method using the three steps to compensate the terrain interferometric phase is presented. After terrain phase compensation, the entire detection flow chart is also presented. The experimental data collected by the Chinese first InSAR system with hybrid baseline (designed by the Institute of Electronics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, IECAS) are used to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Noncoherent integration of HRR RADAR signals for detection of fluctuating targets in non Gaussian clutter using the hough transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In a HRR RADAR where the size of target is larger than wavelength of the RADAR and RADAR range resolution cells, and target returns from different scattering centres of the target produce different patterns in successive scans, make application of traditional methods of clutter suppression inefficient. In this paper, we propose another approach for noncoherent integration of HRR pulses based on the Hough transform which employs the slope-intercept parameter space. By using this method, we do not need to separate clutter from signal and then perform integration. In fact in this method pulse integration, and clutter suppression are done simultaneously. In this paper we investigate the performance of Hough transform-based detector for HRR RADAR signals, in the presence of non Gaussian distributed clutter for non-fluctuating and four types of Swerling targets. The performance of target detection of Hough transform-based detector is analyzed through Monte- Carlo simulation runs.

articleTitle: Efficient construction of training database for identification of aircraft ISAR images
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a new paradigm for classification of aircraft inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) images. A database for identification is efficiently constructed using various 3-D aircraft flight scenarios. Simulation results demonstrate that this method can reduce the memory space for target identification significantly compared to the conventional methodology while maintaining reliable identification performance.

articleTitle: Fast DOA estimation for monostatic MIMO radar with arbitrary array configurations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A fast direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method is presented in this paper for monostatic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with arbitrary array configuration. In order to avoid spectral peaks search in the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm and reduce the computational complexity, the proposed method uses manifold separation and polynomial rooting technique to estimate DOAs of the targets for the monostatic MIMO radar with arbitrary array configurations. The proposed polynomial rooting DOA estimation algorithm provides a lower computation complexity and a better resolution performance than the conventional MUSIC method. Finally, simulation results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: The application of jamming analyzing technique in the radar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In modern warfare, the viability of radar equipments in complex jamming environments becomes a most important index of judging radar capabilities. Its essentiality is nothing less than radar work distance. In this paper, in order to improve radar anti-jamming capabilities, by installing jamming signal receiver circuit in radar received channels, the characteristics of jamming signal are analyzed real-time, the radar work parameters and work modes are altered accordingly. At the same time, radar anti-jamming capabilities can be evaluated by the training mutually of radar and jammer.

articleTitle: Optimum active decoy deployment for effective deception of missile radars
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In a battle engagement scenario, while missile interception and hard kill options can be exercised, soft kill options are less expensive and elegant. In this paper, optimum positioning of an active decoy which is fired in the form of a cartridge from the platform of the target is reported. Various radar and jammer parameters for effective luring away of the missile are studied. Computer simulations are carried out and it is shown that miss distances of the order of half a Kilo meter or more can be obtained for typical monopulse radars.

articleTitle: Target radial velocity estimation robust against additive disturbances for ISAR application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In radar processing, inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) takes advantage of the target rotational motion to provide a 2-D image of the target. The “quality” of this image must be sufficient to be used for target recognition. However, among the main problems to be addressed, the translation motion which is another component of the target motion must be foremost compensated. If this is not the case, a blurred image is obtained. In this paper, we propose a new approach for translation-motion compensation based on the target radial velocity estimation. This method consists in characterizing the radar echoes by several features (mean and wavelet coefficients for instance) and in storing them in sequences which represent the parameter evolution over time. Spectrum analysis methods are then used to get Doppler frequency estimates. To make the estimation robust against additive noise and sea clutter, several estimates are combined to deduce the target radial velocity estimation. Tests on experimental data confirm the validity of the approach.

articleTitle: The integration design of transceiver system of digital array radar based on software-defined radio theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a 10-channel digital array module(DAM) based on software radio theory model is designed for VHF-wave digital array radar. Up to now, DAM has fulfilled all project design requirements.

articleTitle: MIMO SAR/MTI system design and signal analysis for moving target indiction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system is one of the major focuses on research activities for mobile communication. Since late 1990s active studies on MIMO radar system have been done as well. Inspired by recent advances in MIMO radar, the MIMO synthetic aperture radar (SAR) concept was advanced. In this paper,the contradiction between azimuth antenna size (or azimuth resolution) and radar detection range in near space high speed platform SAR/MTI system is analyzed. The technique of multiple -input multiple-output,which can be used to resolve the contradiction, is used in SAR imaging mode. Subsequently, a novel space-time equivalent reconstruction method, which can get a high Performance of detection and location in MTI mode, is presented.
