articleTitle: Knowledge-based signal processing in OTH radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper is concerned with knowledge-based processing technique in high-frequency over the horizon radar (OTHR) to improve radar performance. Knowledge-based processing technique is proposed to increase target detection probability, reduce false alarm in heavy clutter, correct target measurement error and assess battlefield situation. Compared with conventional processing, KB technique really offers the promise of significantly improved performance of OTHR system.

articleTitle: A prototype of High Resolution ISAR imaging system at millimetre-wave band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a prototype of high resolution millimeter-wave ISAR, which is composed of both commercial-off-the-shelf and low-cost designed-specific components. The radar transmits a CWLFM signal in a frequency range from 95.4 to 104.4 GHz, inside a window of atmospheric attenuation. The paper covers both the description of the system components and the assessment of its performance through turntable-imaging experiments. The image formation processor implements the well-known polar formatting algorithm.

articleTitle: One implementation method for beam control subsystem of two dimensional phased array radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Two dimensional phased array radar can scan electronically in two directions of azimuth and elevation. It is the main developing direction of phased array radar. Beam control subsystem is an important part of phased array radar, and it controls the radiation units to achieve the goal of electrical scan. In certain two dimensional phased array radar, the beam control subsystem's main characteristic is that it is divided into multi-levels, which makes the system flexible and convenient to be extended. Each level of the subsystem confronts different radiation units array and is an independent unit. This paper gives a detailed description of the compositions, functions, main technologies and hardware implementation of this beam control subsystem. For raising the performance of the radar, the number of radiation units is becoming more and more, where the request for the Beam control subsystem is more and more difficult to meet.

articleTitle: Design of a miniature wideband radar experimental system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Wideband radars have been found more important both in civil and military applications. Micromation is one key technology for radars mounted at missiles, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV), satellites, etc. The scheme of a miniature wideband radar experimental system is introduced in this paper, while the design and implementation of a wideband signal generator is analyzed in detail. The radar is capable of 0.3m resolution in stripmap mode and implements the function of real time radar echoes acquisition, while it has a slant range of 5km and is no more than 4.5kg in weight. It is fabricated and carried out experiments with the radar mounted at a Cargrador ŏ UAV. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images at finest resolution have been obtained and will also be presented.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband active phased array antenna using open-ended rectangular waveguide as radiating element
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A wideband active phased array antenna using open-ended rectangular waveguide as radiating element is investigated. The results of computation and simulation show the antenna has very high simultaneous bandwidth over 20% and wide beam scanning capabilities up to ±45° in X band. It can be used in very high resolution (better 0.1 m) SAR/GMTI imaging radar.

articleTitle: A one-class-extraction framework for high resolution SAR image classification
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we present a one-class-extraction framework for high resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image classification. The experiment on a TerraSAR-X SAR image shows that the proposed framework provides a promising solution for SAR image classification.

articleTitle: PolSAR image speckle reduction based on polarimetric decomposition and classification
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: On account of the inherent speckle in PolSAR (Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar) images and target scattering properties maintaining after speckle suppressing, an effective algorithm for speckle reduction based on scattering model is developed. First, fast alternative to H/α is used in PolSAR image decomposition, and total back-scattering power is combined for initial p ixel classification. Then, minimum distance measure and h ierarchical cluster method are used for further classification. Finally, pixels are filtered according to their classes. Experimental results with AIRSAR data show that, the new algorithm is more effective than Scattering-Model-Based speckle filter developed by Lee not only in speckle reduction but also in polarimetric properties preservation.

articleTitle: Void-layer detection and depth determination in runways based on GPR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Void-layer detection and thickness determination in runways are studied in this paper. Void-layer is thin layer whose thickness is very small (usually less than 1cm). Firstly, the void-layer can be detected based on its time-frequency distribution characteristic- S transform. This is the first attempt of S transform to be used in the void-layer detection of runways. In the same time, the depth of void-layer can be evaluated based on spectrum optimisation inversion method, in which the impulse pair in the time domain corresponding to the upper and bottom interface of void-layer can be extracted based on the EM wave propagation model and improved system identification method we have proposed in other paper. The simulation results demonstrate the proposed method is valid and the estimation error of thickness is within 5%.

articleTitle: A novel method of ISAR imaging for high speed targets using stepped-frequency chirp waveform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this work, a method of ISAR imaging is proposed for high speed targets using stepped-frequency chirp signal. Keystone formatting is applied among pulses which have identical carrier frequency to eliminate range migration. The range-Doppler coupling and range-profile broadening is compensated by means of processing via Doppler channel division. Simulation results demonstrate the effectivity and adaptability in low SNR condition.

articleTitle: Design of diffractive Cassegrain antenna at W band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, a diffractive Cassegrain antenna for the monopulse radar at W band is designed. The main-reflector of the antenna is divided into several rings, and the surface in each ring is a part of a parabolic reflector with different focal length. The antenna has a gain of 37.6dB and the first sidelobe level is about −18.9dB. The thickness profile of the antenna is less than 10mm on the edge and 30mm in the center. Its radiation performances are comparable with the traditional Cassegrain antenna, but it has a much lower thickness profile.

articleTitle: Phase array antenna pattern design using the minimax algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of beam pattern forming employing the Minimax algorithm. The examples used in this paper demonstrate how phase-only adjustment is performed on both circular and elliptical beams. Compared with complex weights adjustment, problem of phase only adjustment is addressed and performance analysis is provided. A 244 element non-uniformly spaced array antenna is used in this simulation study.

articleTitle: Radar netting technology & its development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Single radar can not excellently complete the mission in the modern war. The information which is required in the modern war can be obtained by radar netting technology. By analyzing the precondition and the realization approach of radar netting technology, the design theory and the key technique for radar netting technology are presented in this paper, and then the new development trends for radar netting technology are also addressed.

articleTitle: Feature aided Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density filter with modified 2D assignment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In order to track multiple targets with time-varying number of targets, the paper proposed a new feature aided Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density (FA-GM-PHD) filter, and adopts a modified 2-D assignment algorithm to carry out the data association and manage the tracks in the FA-GM-PHD filter. The target feature information incorporated into the FA-GM-PHD filter is target Doppler and target down-range extent. With two typical multi-target tracking scenarios, the simulation results in the paper have verified that the FA-GM-PHD filter has much higher correct data association probability and filtering precision of target states than GM-PHD, and it can estimate the number of targets more stably and precisely than GM-PHD. The main shortcoming of FA-GM-PHD is that it has delayed estimate of target's number at the spawning time than GM-PHD, which will be studied in the future work.

articleTitle: Dual-Channel DPCA technique in Bistatic Forward-looking SAR for moving target detection and imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we analyze Dual-Channel Displaced Phase Center Antenna (DPCA) technique in Bistatic Forward-looking SAR (BFSAR) for moving target detection and imaging. In the BFSAR system, the transmitter platform and receiver platform are fixed with two antennas along the direction parallel to the flight track, respectively. It is shown that, using the Dual-Channel DPCA technique in BFSAR, not only the stationary clutter can be suppressed but also the moving target can be focused well. Furthermore, the estimating method of the velocity parameters is also proposed. Lastly, the theoretic analysis is proved by computer simulations.

articleTitle: Through-wall-radar target localization based on random sparse array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Random sparse array is adopted to localize the target in low signal-to-noise ratio case for through-wall-radar. A novel target localization approach is proposed based on multichannel cross-correlation detection and hyperbolic-cross-localization. Simulation results validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Integrated design on digital channelized reconnaissance and jamming
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: With various interlacing signals, the electromagnetic environment of current battlefield becomes more and more dense and complex. It becomes more and more difficult to jam coherent radar especially with the ability of pulse compression. To achieve accurate and effective reconnaissance and jamming against coherent pulse compression radar, a method of integrated design based on digital channelized reconnaissance and jamming is proposed. In the system, the techniques of frequency domain sub-band processing, fractional fourier transform and convolution jamming are used in the design to increase its radar signal detection and denoising capabilities, while the jamming signals generated by a quickly matching method, which are coherent as much as possible, can realize effective jamming.

articleTitle: The accurate model for beam synchronization in spaceborne/airborne hybrid bistatic SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An accurate model for beam synchronization in spaceborne/airborne hybrid bistatic SAR (SA-BSAR) system is proposed. In this model the accurate and real-time steering of receiver's antenna on airborne platform is realized. The main characteristics of this model are proposing the accurate geometric model and applied control model. When the information of antenna's beam on the spaceborne platform can be forecasted or measured, the high precision of the azimuth angle and elevation angle of receiver's antenna is guaranteed. The proposed model could be easily applied and is economic.

articleTitle: Rebar echo detection and suppression in runway using GPR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Strong rebar echo which can't be eliminated in t−x domain directly will disturb the detection and discrimination of the interested targets like cryptic disasters. This paper presents the application of Hyp-curvelet transform in detecting and suppressing rebar echo. Echoes from different targets are concentrated in their own apex coordinate but separated with each other in Hyp-curvelet space after transformed. The peak value in Hyp-curvelet space indicates the location of target. With some discrimination algorithm rebar's location could be obtained, and then its components in Hyp-curvelet space can be eliminated. In this way the reconstructed data will not contain rebar echo. Simulation results show that targets can be detected in low SNR condition, and rebar echo is rarely left over and diseases echoes are hardly any damaged in reconstructed data.

articleTitle: Speckle reduction of SAR image through dictionary learning and point target enhancing approaches
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images are corrupted by speckle noise due to random interference of electromagnetic waves. In this paper, we proposed a speckle reduction technique based on sparse representation and dictionary learning. Firstly, an adaptive dictionary was learned by performing KSVD algorithm through a large amount of training patches extracted from the noisy SAR image. Considering the inaccurate recovery of point targets which is brought by the inadequate number of training samples, we employed a point target enhancing scheme to highlight the important point targets in the SAR image. Some experiments were conducted on real SAR images, and the results shows that our proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the speckle noise as well as preserve details. Some comparisons are made to prove its superiority to the available algorithms.

articleTitle: Adaptive biased weight-based RGPO/RGPI ECCM algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: An adaptive algorithm is presented to counter against the RGPO/RGPI jamming. Using the error range information, a biased weight is updated in every range tracking interval in the presence of the jammer and that the target can be then focused.

articleTitle: Velocity compensation method based on extended Keystone transform for modulated stepped-frequency radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A velocity compensation method based on extended Keystone transform (EKT) for detecting high speed moving target with modulated stepped-frequency radar is presented in this paper. The range migration of target is corrected by EKT and KT, and the range-Doppler coupling and range-profile distortion are compensated by means of processing via Doppler channel division.

articleTitle: MIMO localization by illuminators of opportunity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Passive localization using MIMO techniques has attracted much attention recently. In such schemes, using multiple antennas at transmitter and receiver sides provides spatial diversity without need for identifiable transmitters. On the other hand, one of the problems facing such approach arises when transmitters of a single frequency network (SFN) are used as non-cooperative transmitters and resolving the signals of multiple transmitters reflected from multiple targets is not trivial at receiver side. Therefore, in order to obtain the diversity gain of MIMO localization schemes, it is necessary to develop a technique to assign each echo arriving at the receiver to a given transmitter. In this paper, we propose such technique, that addresses such association problem in an efficient manner.

articleTitle: Azimuth dependence of quadratic range cell migration correction for the high squint synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: For the high squint strip-map mode synthetic aperture radar (SAR), the range cell walk correction (RCWC) in azimuth time domain will bring space-variant along azimuth of quadratic range cell migration. To get the full resolution and quality of the image, the space-variant for the quadratic phase and the quadratic range cell migration in the azimuth must be taken account. In this paper, a novel processing algorithm for the space-variant of quadratic range cell migration is proposed. In the algorithm, the azimuth dependence component of quadratic range cell migration is implemented by the azimuth space-variant filtering in the range frequency domain. After that, the unified quadratic range cell migration can be corrected in the 2-D frequency domain. Simulation and airborne strip-map real data show the accurate and efficient of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Estimation of transition range bin in clutter edge for space time adaptive processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, clutter suppression and target detection in clutter edge is discussed. Firstly the statistical model of the clutter edge is established, based on which maximum likelihood estimation for the transition range bin of the clutter edge is derived. Simulations illustrate that by carefully choosing the secondary samples based on the estimation result of the transition range bin, the signal to inference plus noise ratio (SINR) can be improved significantly.

Author Keywords: estimation of the transition range bin

articleTitle: Identifying the fractional-order systems with frequency responses: A maximum likelihood algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: System modeling plays an important role in radar servo system design with high precision. In this article a maximum likelihood identification algorithm of fractional-order systems with frequency responses is presented. The algorithm is deduced in detail and an equivalent criterion function is obtained from primary likelihood function. Both of the model coefficients and differentiation order estimation are considered in this paper, where two methods of estimating the fractional commensurate order are discussed. One is order scanning method and the other is simultaneous estimation of model coefficients and the differentiation order. Several simulation results are presented, together with the analysis of noise influences.

articleTitle: Research on space target surveillance radar technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, the space debris environment is analyzed, the crucial technology for the design of space surveillance radar is studied, and finally, combined with the actual data, the detection efficiency of radar is simulated and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Development of frequency synthesizer based on DDS+PLL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Phase Locked Loop (PLL) and Direct Digital Frequency synthesis are used widely in the modern frequency synthesis technology. They have their merits and disadvantages respectively. It is feasible to combine the two methods to perform their merits and overcome their disadvantages. The mode of DDS driving PLL is presented to design the frequency synthesizer. The focus of this paper is the hardware implementation, including system elements, key unit circuit design, and phase noise performance of this system is analyzed. Finally, experimental results, which satisfy the design requirements, are introduced.

articleTitle: Airborne bistatic SAR imaging for parallel translational variant configuration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The transmitter and receiver at the difference velocity along parallel trajectories constitutes the parallel translational variant configuration whose echoes have two-dimensional space variant properties. The paper proposes a full analytic imaging algorithm for this configuration in two-dimensional frequency domain. Considering the contribution difference in the Doppler modulation ratio between the transmitter and receiver, their Doppler contribution ratio is used as the weighting factors to derive two-dimensional frequency spectrum of the echo of a target. Utilizing the relations of a target relative to the transmitter and receiver tracks, the spectrum is expressed a uniform formula relative to the receiver track. After compensating the bistatic deformation term, the 2D-CZT is used to correct the residual migration in range and azimuth, thus the focused image is obtained. The simulations validated the 2D-CZT algorithm.

articleTitle: Waveform design with low sidelobe and low correlation properties for MIMO radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: MIMO radar can transmit different signals via different antennas, which enables flexible designs of transmit beampattern. At present, the most methods for beampattern design focus on the spatial performance. In this paper, an approach is proposed to design MIMO radar waveform with beampattern having low sidelobe level and low spatial cross-correlation level, and with the spatial signals having low temporal correlation properties. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Full-polarization scattering center extraction based on Coherent Polarization GTD Model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Full-polarization scattering model and scattering center extraction are studied for high-resolution full-polarization radar systems. A new model called Coherent Polarization Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (CP-GTD) model is proposed and a novel method for full-polarization scattering center extraction is developed. The superiority of the CP-GTD is verified by experiment results.

articleTitle: High resolution imaging with airborne MIMO-SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper describes a modified MIMO-SAR ω-k algorithm integrating with motion compensation to achieve high resolution. Firstly, a model of motion error for airborne MIMO-SAR system was established. Then improved Stolt-mapping was proposed to separate Range Cell Migration Correction (RCMC) and azimuth focus, and the motion error was corrected by two steps of compensation. Finally, sub-bands were combined into a whole band in spatial-frequency domain to obtain high range resolution. Simulation examples are provided to verify the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Diagonally loaded space-time adaptive detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, the concept of space-time adaptive detection (STAD) is presented. The diagonally loaded adaptive matched filter (DL-AMF) and the diagonally loaded adaptive coherence estimation (DL-ACE) are analyzed. Their performance is investigated, and the asymptotically analytical expression of the probability of false alarm (PFA) and the probability of detection (PD) are derived. Compared to the AMF and the ACE, the PD's of the DL-AMF and the DL-ACE are improved dramatically, especially when the sample support is limited.

articleTitle: Ocean dynamic information obtaining based on SAR ocean images matching
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Obtaining ocean surface information is one of the most important applications in the ocean remote sensing field. Current movement and ocean wave transmission are crucial constituent part of ocean dynamic information. Image matching is an indispensable step to get the dynamic information through SAR sequential images. In this paper, two matching methods are proposed according to different SAR sequential images. To SAR ocean sub-aperture sequential images, the time interval between images is very short. We believe there is approximately a rigid movement between sequential images, so we then propose an improved Phase Correlation Method to match images. Experimental results show that the optimized method presents 1/10 pixel accuracy and good noise robustness. To the long time interval (15 minutes) images, shape deformation is presented between sequential images. Thus we propose to adopt a special deformation tolerant matching method in this paper to tackle the problem. After matching, according to movement direction and quantity, we can get ocean dynamic information of ocean wave moving tendency.

articleTitle: Study on method of selecting meter-wave resonance radar operation frequency point based on ADBF
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a method of selecting operation frequency point based on adaptive beam forming. It is firstly to reject the directional interference by spatial filtering, then select suitable operation frequency point. The simulation results shows feasibility and effectiveness of this scheme.

articleTitle: Joint fading coefficient and DOA estimation with known waveforms in multipath environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We consider maximum likelihood (ML) estimation of the direction of arrival (DOA) and fading coefficients in multipath environment when the incident signal have known waveforms. A efficient iterative algorithm based on alternating maximization technique has been presented and Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for ML estimator is also obtained. Finally, numerical examples are illustrated to assess the performance of the proposed ML estimator and make comparisons with existing alternatives.

articleTitle: Wideband scaled Radon-Fourier transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: With respect to the scale effect of wideband radar echoes, this paper proposes a long-time coherent integration method, i.e., wideband scaled Radon-Fourier transform (WSRFT). It can make great improvement on the detection performance of far-range, weak and high speed target of wideband radar. The degradation of pulse compression performance caused by scale effect is studied. Range and velocity shifts of the output of standard RFT (SRFT) are analyzed. Furthermore, the detection performance comparison between WSRFT and SRFT is investigated. Finally, detailed numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed WSRFT.

articleTitle: A novel CFAR threshold estimated method for coherent integration detector of PD radar seeker
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Because of the imperfect model of the clutter, as well as the limited samples, there is always a wide performance gap between the theoretical model and the practical result for the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detector of coherent radar in Range-Doppler domain. A novel method of estimating the detection threshold is proposed in this paper. The method is based on the least square criteria and derived from the relationship between the CFAR detection threshold and the probability of false alarm. Simulation results confirm the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Results of the LORAMbis bistatic VHF/UHF SAR experiment for FOPEN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: LORAMbis is a joint research program involving FOI (Sweden) and ONERA (France). The objective is to evaluate the performance of low frequency bistatic SAR for clutter reduction in under-foliage target detection. This paper presents the SAR bistatic system and a few campaign results.

articleTitle: Hyper parameter estimation in MRF-based SAR chip image segmentation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: SAR chip image segmentation is a key step in SAR automatic target recognition (ATR). Aiming at this challenging task, many available methods are proposed. Among these methods, MRF-based segmentation is the most popular one. MRF-based method for SAR chip image segmentation is more like an inverse-filter which tries to smooth noise. The hyper parameter determines its capability of noise reduction. The larger the hyper parameter, the more noise is smoothed. However, when the hyper parameter gets large, some interested regions may be regarded as noise and be smoothed. In order to smooth all noise and preserve interested regions, the hyper parameter should be carefully selected. In this paper, by rewriting the regularization term in MRF-based SAR chip image segmentation, we find its similarity with total variation (TV) filtering. Moreover, some sort of analytic expression of TV regularization hyper parameter has been derived. According to this similarity, we are convinced that these analytic results of hyper parameter estimation in TV filtering may be carefully extended to MRF-based SAR chip image segmentation. A core concept in these expressions is ‘scale’ which refers to the area-perimeter ratio of interested regions. However, when it comes to MRF-based SAR chip image segmentation, the ‘scale’ has to be redefined. In our study, we redefine the ‘scale’ and illustrate scales of some canonical shapes. Finally, these formulations of MRF hyper parameter are validated by simulated data.

articleTitle: Ship target recognition using high resolution range profiles based on FMT and SVM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presented here introduces a technique for automatic recognition of ship targets from high range resolution range profiles. The technique incorporates Fourier-Mellin transform (FMT) and support vector machine (SVM) to identify ship targets. According to the shift invariance of the Fourier transform and scale invariance of the Mellin transform, the high resolution range profiles are processed using FMT to form the feature vectors. Within the recognizer, the multi-class SVM is used based on binary tree, which can reduce the number of SVM classifiers and repetitive training samples effectively. The recognition results from simulation data and measurement data of ship target range profiles prove the validity and robustness of the method proposed.

articleTitle: Experimental results of spaceborne stripmap SAR raw data imaging via compressed sensing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Compressed sensing (CS) is a new theory that enables sampling below the Nyquist rate, while the quality of reconstruction is guaranteed. This theory is applied to sparse circumstance. Based on this theory, this paper proposes a feasible method for the spaceborne stripmap synthetic aperture radar (SAR) raw data imaging. The technique presented is introduced as an alternative option to the traditional matched filtering. An experiment with SAR raw data is also described. Its purpose is to show that CS can be applied to spaceborne stripmap SAR raw data.

articleTitle: Optimization of spatial filter for DPI and multipath interferences in passive radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Spatial smoothing technique is an effective spatial filtering to eliminating the direct path interference(DPI) and multipath interfere-ences in passive radar based on opportunity of illuminators, such as FM broadcast transmitter. The optimal weights are often acquired with respect to subarrays. This fact implies that there are extra adaptive degrees of freedom to be unused to improve the performance of spatial smoothing adaptive array. A novel spatial filter based on secondary optimization for spatial smoothing is proposed in the paper. We show how to optimize the adaptive array such that the pattern of array can minimize white noise power and match desired respond. Simulation results by applying real collected data show the proposed method is superior detect performance in comparison with conventional spatial smoothing.

articleTitle: Detection probability of early warning radar against hypersonic cruise missile
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Detection probability against hypersonic cruise missile is a key factor to assess early warning radar performance. Based on the search theory, detection probability models of early warning radar for hypersonic cruise missile are set up respectively in the case of no target indication, missile azimuth and motion state indication. Take PAVE PAWS radar for example, detection probability of the three conditions above is solved. The research process can apply to design and evaluate the early warning radar.

articleTitle: SAR image despeckling method based on dual-tree complex wavelet
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We propose a despeckling method based on dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) for SAR image. The Gaussian model is used to model the non-logarithmic additive noise of the local isotropic region. Shrinkage function is obtained with maximum a posteriori estimation.

articleTitle: Target classification system based on the characterization of targets by subspaces
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a novel classification technique based on targets bistatic backscattering coefficients acquired at low frequencies. Each target class is characterized by a subspace. Air targets are then classified based on geometrical classification criteria. An average recognition rate of 90% is achieved.

articleTitle: An evaluation method for sparse microwave imaging radar system using phase diagrams
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: We propose a method based on the phase diagram tool to evaluate the sparse microwave imaging radar system. In the method, success rates of signal recovery are derived from the statistics of relative errors between the targets and the recovered signals. Success rates for each combination of SNR, sparsity and sampling ratio are provided to form a three-dimensional phase diagram. We demonstrate that the trend of success rates is presented accurately by taking advantage of phase transition boundary. These ideas are efficient strategy to analysis and design the sparse microwave imaging radar system.

articleTitle: Image formation algorithm with motion compensation for forward-looking bistatic SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The paper concentrates on image formation method for the practical forward-looking bistatic SAR (FL-BiSAR). In the FL-BiSAR configuration presented in the paper, the transmitter operates in the broadside mode, while the receiver is dynamic toward the target. In practical applications, however, the platforms cannot maintain constant velocity or move with acceleration. Considering the influence to form image, the actual aperture is split into subapertures. It is reasonably assumed the platforms move with constant acceleration vector in a subaperture when the subaperture is small enough. The equivalent bistatic squint range model incorporating three-dimensional acceleration and velocity is deduced. Based on this model, an improved CS algorithm with new phase compensation factors for FL-BiSAR is proposed. The simulation results show that the imaging quality processed by the proposed method is close to the value of the BP algorithm.

articleTitle: Reduced-dimensional ESPRIT algorithm for MIMO radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A reduced-dimensional (RD) ESPRIT algorithm is proposed to reduce the dimension of the received data and to estimate the DOAs of multiple targets for arbitrary MIMO radar linear array configuration. It exploits the rotational invariance property of the RD virtual array and has much lower computational complexity than the methods of the same kind.

articleTitle: A BOT algorithm based on sliding window n-step forward prediction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Bearing-only tracking (BOT) involves nonlinearity. Extended Kalman filter (EKF) is usually employed for the advantages of efficient computation and real time operation. However, the observability badly declines at a high observation rate, which degrades the filtering performance. In order to address this issue, a BOT algorithm based on sliding window n-step forward prediction is proposed. It enhances the observability effectively, and improves the performance of BOT filter at a high observation rate. Target tracking experiments under different scenarios show that the proposed algorithm has good accuracy and stability, and is suitable for application at a high observation rate.

articleTitle: Image segmentation using Directionlet-domain hidden Markov tree models
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we modeled the Directionlet coefficients of an image using hidden Markov tree (HMT) model and obtained the image segmentation results using model parameter training, multi-scale likelihood computation and the background of neighborhood-based maximum posterior probability. We demonstrate the performance of the proposed method with synthetic mosaic images and SAR images. The experiment results showed that our method obtained more exact boundary and uniform regions.

articleTitle: Extraction and analysis of structural features of ships in high resolution SAR images
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Ship classification in high resolution SAR satellite imagery is a hotspot and preceding problem in SAR applications. According to the different features of cargo ship, oil tanker and container ship in high resolution SAR images, we propose a method to extract structure feature of three civilian ship types. Firstly, the morphological pre-processing is used for sidelobe suppression. Secondly, the main axes are extracted using Hough Transform; the Minimum Enclosing Rectangle(MER) of ship is obtained and rotated to the direction of principal axes, then it is adjusted to fit the ship well. Finally, the scattering properties of different ship types are analyzed. The result shows that this method has good performance in feature extraction of ships in high resolution SAR imagery.

articleTitle: Compressive sensing for ground penetrating radar imaging based on random filtering
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Sparse signals can be reconstructed from a small set of measurements basing on the theory of compressive sensing (CS), whereas the key points are the selection of the measurement matrix and the reconstruction algorithm. This paper presents an imaging algorithm for ground penetrating radar based on CS. The measurement matrix is selected via random filters, which can reduce the number of nonzero elements in the measurement matrix effectively. We adopt the simple orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm to reconstruct signal with less data storage and lower computational complexity. Simulation results are provided to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Airborne bistatic SAR echo simulator based on Multi-GPU platform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar(SAR) echo simulator plays an important role in the development, debugging and performance evaluation of radar system. In this paper, an airborne bistatic SAR echo simulation algorithm based on CUDA architecture is proposed. Then a parallel computing platform with GPUs controlled by CPU threads is presented to achieve the echo simulator. The results show that the speed of the echo simulator based on Multi-GPU is 300 times faster than CPU. Multi-GPU platform has the advantage of computing parallelism, which greatly improves the speed of SAR signal processing.

articleTitle: A new reduced-dimension GSC for target tracking and interference suppression
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To deal with the beam tracking issue in phased array when interferences are removed by adaptive beamforming, a new generalized sidelobe canceller(GSC) that can realize beam tracking is proposed in this paper. First of all, with the estimated angles and the current training samples, it constructs a new reduced-dimension blocking matrix with the number of interferences as the number of columns, which is realized through linear combinations of column vectors in the array covariance matrix, without eigen-decomposition. Then the reduced-dimension blocking matrix is worked on both sum and difference beams, estimating adaptive sum and difference weights and realizing the anti-jamming exporting. Finally, it realizes beam tracking through the monopulse technology. This reduced-dimension generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC) can suppress interferences effectively when tracking the target, with the advantages of simple structure, less computation and little distortion of monopulse ratio curve. The processing results of simulation and measured data show the effectiveness and advantages of this reduced-dimension generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC).

articleTitle: A low-cost MIMO radar system concept based on single transmitter and single receiver
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a novel low-cost time-division multiplexing MIMO radar system concept by using only one transmitter and one receiver. For an MIMO radar system of M-element transmitting array and N-element receiving array, the number of required transmitters/receivers is reduced from N+M to 2 for considerable cost reduction.

articleTitle: High resolution radar imaging using sparse signal representation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In this paper, we present a new method for high resolution radar imaging. Based on ideal point-scattering model, a sparse representation algorithm via smoothed l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> norm is introduced to achieve high-resolution radar imaging. The experimental results validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Air defense antimissile target identification system architecture based on operational view
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Aiming at air defense antimissile identification of target in wide airspace and complex battlefield environment, this paper adopts the Activity Based Methodology(ABM) to model the top-level architecture based on the operational view(OV) of the Dept. of Defense Architecture Framework(DoDAF) standard, including creating several core products of OV. The feasibility and guidance of this method for complex system design and construction is proved through analyzing.

articleTitle: A broadband antenna with aperture-coupled feed
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A broadband antenna with aperture-coupled feed is proposed. With adjusted parameters, it exhibits a broad impedance bandwidth (VSWR ≤ 2) of about 60% (7GHz–13GHz). The proposed antenna is composed of two circle radiation elements fed by microstrip line and a step-shaped slot on the ground plane. The results show that the proposed antenna has a broad impedance bandwidth of about 60%. Along with the broad impedance bandwidth, the radiation pattern and gain of the antenna is investigated and discussed.

articleTitle: Interacting multiple model target tracking algorithm based on particle filtering
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The movement model of maneuvering targets is analyzed, and based on the fact that the interacting multiple models in extended Kalman Filter and Unscented Kalman Filter have a low precision of tracking strong maneuvering targets, particle filter is introduce into interacting multi-model, so that particle filtering of every model can be realized through particle filtering algorithm. The simulation result shows that particle filtering algorithm has improved the tracking precision of strong and nonlinear maneuvering targets.

articleTitle: Motion compensation in post-PFA domain for high resolution spotlight SAR imagery
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A novel motion compensation (MoCo) algorithm for high resolution (HR) spotlight SAR imagery is proposed. It is capable of correcting both phase error and range cell migration (RCM) in the post-PFA data domain. It is a robust way to estimate phase error by Map-drift (MD) method, including range-invariant and range-variant ones. What is more, the random characteristic of RCM is also taken into consideration to achieve a well aligned range profile data. Finally, series experimental results are listed to validate the proposal.

articleTitle: Cooperative target localization and tracking for random sparse array through-wall-radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: To improve the precision of target localization and tracking, a novel through-wall-radar system based on random sparse array is developed and an approach of cooperative target localization and tracking is proposed. Simulation results validate the approach for the novel system.

articleTitle: An improved FOCUSS algorithm for multi-channel FMCW radar imaging of distributed targets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: In a Frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar system with multi-channel antenna array, the high resolution imaging of distributed targets is studied here. Motivated by the clustering property of the targets, we proposed a Clustering FOCUSS method by incorporating an additional clustered constraint into the solution of the FOCal Underdetermined System Solver (FOCUSS) algorithm. It is shown in the simulation for distributed targets scenario that the novel algorithm gets better performance in respect of imaging accuracy compared with methods of Capon beamforming, the L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm algorithm and the FOCUSS algorithm.

articleTitle: SAR raw data 2-D imaging model and simulation of GEOCSAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Geosynchronous circular SAR (GeoCSAR) is a novel system combined with GeoSAR and the Circular SAR (CSAR). The daily track of GeoCSAR is an inclined ellipse, while we divided the total aperture into several sub-apertures. Based on 2-D SAR image of sub-aperture we can observe the same place continuously. While the aperture is disturbed by perturbations and could not be approximated as a line. This paper discuss the precise imaging model of GeoCSAR, and simulates the corresponding raw data of point target and distributed target.

articleTitle: Consecutive images formation for airborne SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper analyzes the SAR consecutive images formation for different trajectory selection and derives the range and azimuth geometric distortion induced by the trajectory deviation. Then a method is proposed for correcting the geometric distortion to form consecutive SAR images.

articleTitle: Robust D-InSAR deformation phase estimation method using joint processing of neighboring pixels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A robust D-InSAR deformation phase estimation method is proposed. The method can accomplish the images auto-coregistration by using joint processing of multiple pixels and the phase noise suppression by using signal subspace fitting. The performance is investigated using simulated data.

Author Keywords: complex interfrometric phase joint data vector

articleTitle: P band SAR narrow band RFI suppression methods research
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This work aims at P band SAR narrow band RFI question, we discussed trap wave method, eigen subspace method and LMS method, the result of point target imaging simulation proved that modern signal processing methods are superiority over traditional trap wave method.

articleTitle: An analysis on error sources of guidance radar detection performance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Target detection is the premise of identification/tracking of the guidance radar. There are many factors affect the detection performance of the guidance radar. Analysis and research the error sources is the basis of performance evaluation and system optimization design for guidance radar, and it provides technical support for the target detection performance evaluation and further testing and optimization of the guidance radar's signal processing algorithms. This paper analyzes and researches the error sources of guidance radar from the target, clutter characteristics and motion characteristics of radar platform, the simulation results show correctness of the analysis.

articleTitle: Study on underwater acoustic simulation measurement of radar HRRP for ship targets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The measurement of the high resolution range profile (HRRP) of ship targets is an important and complex problem. It is urgently settled in radar detection and target recognition research field. In this paper, the method of the underwater acoustic field simulation instead of the electromagnetic field to measure targets' HRRP had been researched. The comparability between target acoustic scattering and electromagnetic scattering is studied and the theoretical analysis is proposed for underwater acoustic measurement experiments. The results of the experiments show that the method of underwater acoustic simulation to measure water surface targets' HRRP is valid.

articleTitle: Sea state parameters extraction from radar images: System design and implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The main concentration of this paper is the system design and implementation of sea state parameters retrieval technique from nautical radar. The system consists of three main components: a general sea clutter data acquisition subsystem, a standard computer and a software package. The data acquisition subsystem is designed to acquire sea clutter data and then form consecutive image sequence for further analysis. The standard computer stores the acquired data and offers a hardware platform for the entire system. The software package with program language of Visual C++ fulfills the realization of the retrieval algorithms. Experimental results show the effectiveness and feasibility of the research. This work has significant values not only for ocean engineering but also for the performance of radar system in the detection of dim targets in strong sea clutter.

articleTitle: System-level simulation of the full-polarimetric radar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A system-level simulation model has been developed to conduct the simulation of a whole full-polarimetric radar system, all parameters both in analogue part and digital part can then be optimally selected, thus the most optimal radar performance can be achieved.

articleTitle: Spatial localization of quasi-stationary targets using bistatic MIMO radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Quasi-stationary targets (QST) represent a class of nonstationary targets in which the statistics of their echoes are locally static over a short period of time, but exhibit differences from one local time frame to another. A novel algorithm is proposed for spatial localization of quasi-stationary targets using bistatic MIMO radar. The proposed algorithm exploits the character of quasi-stationary targets and the rotational0 invariance property of ESPRIT to estimate the two-dimensional direction of departures (2-D DODs) and two-dimensional direction of arrivals (2-D DOAs) of quasi-stationary targets, so the targets can be localized in a 3-D plane. The algorithm does not refer to multi-dimensional nonlinear peak search, so that the computational load of the algorithm is low, and the estimated parameters of the targets can be paired automatically. The theoretical analysis and simulation results show the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: A new method for ionospheric clutter suppression in HFSWR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: High frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) is an effective early warning radar, but the detection performance is impacted by the ionospheric clutter seriously. In order to suppress the ionospheric clutter, a segment accumulation algorithm is proposed, based on the time-frequency characteristics of the ionospheric clutter. The time-domain data of radar echo is divided into several segments, and the frequency spectrum was estimated with amplitude and phase estimation (APES) in each subsegment. The amplitudes fluctuate fast and huge contains the most ionospheric clutter. The time-domain ionospheric clutter is reconstructed and subtracted from the original signal. By processing the measured data, it shows that the method can effectively improve the SNCR (signal to noise and clutter ratio) in the detection unit polluted by the ionospheric clutter.

articleTitle: Planar array ISAR imaging and anti-jamming performance analyzation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) is a technique to generate a two-dimensional high resolution image of a target. In situations where other radars display only a single unidentifiable bright moving pixel, the ISAR image is often adequate to discriminate between various missiles, military aircraft, and civilian aircraft. It can improve the signal to noise ratios (SNR) using planar array antenna configuration. The imaging geometry of the planar array ISAR was shown firstly. Then signal processing flow was expounded, and the minimum entropy method was proposed to align the range signal from different receive antenna elements. The spatially variant apodization was used to eliminating sidelobes. The anti-jamming performance of the planar array ISAR was analyzed. Simulations were executed in the end and all results illustrated the superiority of the planar array ISAR.

articleTitle: Modeling and suppression of clutter for airborne fire control radar with conformal antennas array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Conformal antennas array (CAA) offer many advantages over conventional planar antennas array (PAA) such as less payload weight, larger effective aperture and increased field of view without mechanically canting or rotating the array. In this paper, airborne fire control radar (AFCR) with CAA is analyzed in terms of antennas modeling, working mechanism, subarray synthesis, clutter characteristics and clutter suppression method, etc. Firstly, the mathematics model and geometry configuration of AFCR with CAA are given, and the manners of subarray division and working are obtained based on the requirement for moved target detection of AFCR, and the pattern properties of CAA are analyzed. Secondly, the clutter spectrum distribution in space-time plane is analyzed. Finally, clutter suppression performance of existing space-time adaptive processing (STAP) techniques for practice is compared, and the minimum detectable velocity of AFCR with CAA is shown.

articleTitle: Bistatic sar data focusing using an analytical spectrum based frequency scaling algorithm in tandem configuration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: A bistatic frequency scaling algorithm (FS) is proposed based on an exact analytical bistatic point target (PT) spectrum obtained by a geometry-based bistatic formula (GBF) method in tandem configuration. Since numerical calculation is no longer needed when calculating the important parameter- the half quasi bistatic angle (HQBA), fast imaging process is achieved. Unlike the existing algorithms, it avoids the influence of the baseline to range ratio because of its precise spectrum, it can handle the bistatic data with a large baseline. The proposed method has been proved by using simulated data. By comparing the experimental results between the proposed method and the numerical calculation method which has a heavy computational burden, the images were almost the same, which further proves the advantages and correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Copula method constant modulus waveform synthesis for MIMO radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: MIMO radar is a new promising research area. In MIMO radar in compare to conventional phase array radar each radar antenna can transmit arbitrary waveform. This degree of freedom in waveforms design brings numerous benefits for MIMO radar. But to deploy these benefits, a waveform optimization problem should be solved. One of the most important criteria in designing waveforms is achieving prescribed correlation matrix. In this paper we propose a novel stochastic method based on copula for constant modulus waveform synthesis to obtain a given correlation matrix. This method is compared to existing methods for pros and cons. Simulation is carried to verify the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Knowledge-aided small target tracking
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper presents a novel method to track small targets via combining priori knowledge with NNCJPDA as data association and track management strategies. Simulation results show that the track detection probability is improved by about 20 percent with this method.

articleTitle: Cost-effective real-time motion compensation of airborne UWB SAR based on single GPS receiver and PGA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: The paper presents a cost-effective real-time motion compensation (MOCO) strategy of airborne UWB SAR based on single GPS receiver and Phase Gradient Autofocus (PGA). The real-time imaging result is present to validate its feasibility.

articleTitle: Range-velocity synchronous gate-pull radar jamming suppression with instantaneous cross-correlation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: This paper analyses the characteristics of range-velocity synchronous gate-pull radar jamming, and propose a suppression method with instantaneous cross-correlation based on signal model. The simulation results accord with the theoretical analysis and confirm its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Ballistic target discrimination based on polarimetric entropy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 2011 IEEE CIE International Conference on Radar
abstract: Polarimetric entropy derived from the Cloude-Pottier decomposition is widely applied to fully polarimetric SAR images for target unsupervised discrimination and classification. In this paper, an algorithm for discriminating ballistic targets based on polarimetric entropy is studied. Using the fully polarimetric narrowband target echoes, polarimetric entropy is extracted to represent the randomness of target scattering characteristic in temporal domain. Based on the different polarimetric entropy values of warhead and decoy, the discrimination method is put forward. Lastly, simulations are performed using the measured data of a scaled target, whose results prove the effectiveness of this algorithm.
